**LS-19 — `read_view` is the one true channel.** Pure, side-effect free, callable from `validate`, P3 and presentation; it may call `ensure_derived()` (a rebuild of non-hashed caches), which keeps `validate`'s hash-unchanged guarantee. **`ensure_derived()` is eager** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: every structural mutator (M1–M6, M19) and `post_restore` finishes by rebuilding the derived caches, so a read never triggers a rebuild in an arbitrary presentation frame (the weld-preview drag calls pure `can_join` against caches that are already derived) and the lazy call remains only as a no-op guard. **Return shapes on the hot path** are typed scalar getters (`compartment_p(cid)`, `compartment_t(cid)`, `node_hp(id)`, `served_pm(id)`, …) or one reusable view object per kind that the caller must read before its next call; the Dictionary-shaped returns listed below are for tests, the Debug Overlay and cold paths. `failures(filter)` returns index slices of the per-step columnar descriptor store (preallocated parallel packed arrays, one slot per live descriptor) and allocates nothing. Queries: `compartment(cid)` → `{V, n_o2, n_inert, P, p_o2, o2_pm, T, band_o2, band_p, band_t, pressure_trend, fuel_puddle_ml, status}`; `compartment_at(room_ref)`; `node(id)` / `edge(id)` → `{state, hp, hp_cap, forced_mode, served_pm, stock, flow, sev, warn_elapsed}`; `loop_component(loop, any_node)` → `{pool, cap, supply, demand, sat_by_tier[5], members}`; `failures(filter)` → sorted `FailureDescriptor[]`; `power_use(section_id)` → `{draw_w, delta_w_last5, lamps_lit_w, noisy_w}` (Attention's stimulus); `served_pm(node_id)` (lamp brightness = base × served / 1000); `can_join(plan)`; `neighbors(cid)`, `nodes_in(cid)`, `section_of(id)`; `alarm_sections()` → ascending, duplicate-free `section_id`s owning an `alarm_eligible` descriptor in the last committed run (LS-13 (c)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; `summary()`; `true_value(kind, id)` — the unfiltered value, which the Perception Filter is the only non-diagnostic reader allowed to wrap; `block_hash()`. There is no "perceived" variant anywhere in the Graph.

**LS-19 additions** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query, in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view, attention-system, ship-section-and-layout-data-model, adaptive-audio-and-tells, ship-body-and-interior-physics, save-load-and-versioned-format, debug-overlay-true-values)*. `node(id)` also returns `stock_pm` (`⌊1000 × stock / capacity⌋`, capacity = the def's `cap_ml`, `BATT_CELL` or the O2_TANK template maximum), `switch_pos` (a CABLE_JUNCTION's `breaker_closed`; a VALVE edge's `open` through `edge(id)`), the request fields `req_w` / `throttle_pm` / `out_w`, and `run_pm` (0..1000): 0 when the requested load is 0 (LOAD `req_w` 0, SCRUBBER `req_w` 0, PUMP `throttle_pm` 0, REACTOR `out_w` 0) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, otherwise `served_pm` for a consumer (a SCRUBBER's `run_pm` is `served_pm` while its request is above 0; a scrubber throttled to free tank space is still running and is not dimmed by the throttle, and its O2 output is D.5's concern, not `run_pm`) — except a HEATER, whose `run_pm` is `⌊duty_t × served_pm / 1000⌋` (0 while its thermostat is satisfied, although its `req_w` stays 500) — and `⌊1000 × out_w / out_w_rated⌋` for a REACTOR; this is also the D.9 `duty_pm`, so duty wear stops on a switched-off pump, a satisfied heater and a reactor at `out_w` 0 (the first draft keyed duty wear to `served_pm`, which reads 1000 for a machine switched off on a met tier) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `opening(edge_id)` → `{area, area_max, door_state}` for stored OPENINGs (`door_state` derived from `area`: CLOSED at 0, OPEN at `area_max`, PARTIAL between). `open_ends(node_id)` → the port indices with `open_end`. `stress_active(section_id)` = `step_no < stress_until_step` (the STRESS armed state). `draw_grant(crew_id)` → `{requested, granted}` is the M15 grant applied at the last phase 0 (the table is persisted, LS-21, so a restore between hook ticks returns the same grant) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `hull_segments_of(compartment_id)` lists a room's hull segments (the Graph has no pixel geometry; a nearest-point query is Layout's). `soonest_warning_remaining(loaded_only)` → ticks `(W_MIN_STEPS − warn_elapsed) × GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, minimum over live descriptors whose gate is still closed, skipping dormant sections when `loaded_only` (a dormant section freezes `warn_since_step`, so its descriptors would never close). `compartment_at` for an actor whose `actor_section` is NONE returns the exterior's atmosphere (`n_o2` 0, no pressure), never the last compartment's. `true_value(kind, id)` kinds are the In-World Instruments IW-9 set — `p_o2`, `P`, `T` (compartment), `stock_pm` (node), `supply`, `demand` (POWER component) — plus `hp` for diagnostics. `loop_component(POWER, node)`: `supply` = `S + D` (D.6 `avail`, W this step), `demand` = `Σ R_k` (requested W, inrush included); Instruments' `load = ⌊1000 × demand / max(1, supply)⌋` is its own reading, not `ρ`, and reads no `cap`. `power_use(section_id)`, all in W per step for the section's consumers, recomputed in phase 2: `draw_w` = Σ served W (all tiers, lamps and inrush included, battery charge excluded); `delta_w_last5` = `draw_w` now − `draw_w` five runs ago (signed; lamps included — D.6 Example C's 1200 W contains its 300 W of lamps; `post_restore` seeds the window flat, so it reads 0 after a load); `lamps_lit_w` = Σ served W of LOAD subtype LAMP, including any LAMP node such as `bcn_main` (the Graph does not know a beacon, so its 20 W step is in `delta_w_last5` too); `noisy_w` = Σ served W of SCRUBBER, PUMP, HEATER and DOOR_MOTOR nodes (lamps excluded). `o2_pm`, `n_o2` and `n_inert` have no dirty-key quantum of their own: they ride the `C/<cid>` key fired by the `P` (10 dkPa) and `p_o2` (5 dkPa) buckets and stay exact in `read_view`.

**LS-20 — Dirty keys confirm `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`.** Keys are ints `(KIND << 32) | id` with KIND ∈ {COMP 1, BAND 2, NODE 3, EDGE 4, DESC 5, LOOP 6, SEAM 7, TOPO 8, SECTION 9} (written in this document by their family names `C/<cid>`, `B/<cid>`, `N/<id>`, `F/<id>`, `L/<loop>/<anchor>`, `S/<seam_id>`, `T`, `SEC/<id>`); no String is built per key per run. Rules: continuous values never dirty per step — a key fires only when `⌊value / quantum⌋` changes bucket (quanta: `T` 1000 mC, `P` 10 dkPa, `p_o2` 5 dkPa, store 20 ‰, intensity 100 ‰, `hp` 250 bp); one `C/<cid>` per compartment per step, not one per field, fired when the `T`, `P` **or** `p_o2` bucket changed (three triggers, not `P` alone) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; structural change uses `T` + `SEC/<id>`, never per-node keys; last-emitted buckets are derived and `post_restore` seeds them so a restore yields one `ALL` and then silence; Instruments read values only through `perceived` and the honest needle moves on LS-20 quantum crossings as a one-step ramp (In-World Instruments IW-11); Failure & Trail polls once per Graph step and reads a per-step cache every frame (FT-15); Adaptive Audio reads per Graph step — keys wake discrete presentation only (trail spawn/despawn, loop on/off) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view, failure-and-trail-system)*. D.10 bounds the worst designed cascade at 38 (MVP) and 135 (VS-A) keys, so **`MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 stays as registered**; the Graph confirms it and asks that it never fall below 128 (MVP's worst case is 38; VS-A's 135 already exceeds 128) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Alternative considered:* SD's string-keyed families — the semantics are identical; the int encoding is chosen for the per-run allocation cost at VS-A (ADR-LSG-06). The kernel's key type is a 64-bit int (ADR-0004); composite family ids such as `L/<loop>/<anchor>` are packed by the Graph into the 32-bit id (the packing and its range check are fixed by ADR-0011) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0004 sync)*.

**LS-21 — Serialization, hash, summary, interchange.** *Persisted (canonical):* `schema_version`, `next_node_id`, `next_edge_id`, `next_seam_id`, `next_section_id`, `last_step_no` and the per-hook cursors `last_step_power`, `last_step_atmo`, `last_step_failure` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the `def_table` CSR pair (`def_off`, `def_utf8`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; nodes and edges with every field of LS-3/LS-5 including tombstones; SeamRecords; sections with `dormant`, `dormant_since_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, `rate_pm`, `stress_pm`, `stress_until_step`, `vented_mgu`, `radiated_dj`, `spilled_cool_ml`, `produced_mgu`, `breathed_mgu`, `produced_dj`, `burned_uml`, `spilled_heat_mdj` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `discarded_*`, `withdrawn_*` (M16, per medium) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from web-map-and-transit)*; compartments `layout_room_ref`, `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `T`, `t_rem`, `fuel_puddle_ml` and the hysteresis memory `band_o2`, `band_p`, `band_t`, `p_prev` (the previous run's `P`), and the warn trackers `warn_since_o2`, `warn_since_p`, `warn_since_t` (i32 each) and `warn_bits` (u8) — payload row order after `p_prev` (+13 bytes per compartment as raw array elements, 65 for the MVP five; the encoder's per-array tag and count header is extra) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; every stored OPENING's `strain_gas` and `strain_heat` live bits (SEAL_STRAIN hysteresis, D.14); **and the three input queues** — `pending_draw` (compartment, crew, mGU), `pending_load` (node, `req_w`) and `pending_trace` (kind, subject, magnitude), each in arrival order and bounded (draw ≤ `MAX_CREW` × compartments, load ≤ 64, trace ≤ `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`), plus the last applied `draw_grant` table. A snapshot can be taken on any tick, so a queue that held a breath, a trace or a load change between two hook ticks would otherwise be lost on restore and the restored run would diverge from the uninterrupted one *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Derived, never in a snapshot:* `V`, `exposed_tiles` (from Layout), components, trees, `path_cap`, degrees, id → slot maps, `served_pm`, descriptors, `P`/`p_o2`/`o2_pm`, last-emitted buckets, the cached hash. Rule: anything the next step depends on that is not re-derivable from persisted fields is persisted (`t_rem`, `tc_rem`, `fuel_rem`, `out_w`, `forced_mode_next`, `warn_since_step` with its `has_warn` bit, `thaw_until_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, the GA-T fields `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` and `isolated_at_step`, `dormant_since_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, the three `pending_*` queues, the band and SEAL_STRAIN memory, the compartment warn trackers `warn_since_o2/p/t` and `warn_bits` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*); `served_pm` is not, because phase 2 recomputes it before use. The Graph publishes no byte writer: its `snapshot()` payload is a Dictionary of named `PackedInt64Array` / `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedByteArray` fields (tombstones inside the arrays; the `def_off` / `def_utf8` CSR pair) and the kernel's `CanonicalEncoder` encodes it (PACKED tag 0x09, one `to_byte_array()` copy per array, no interpreted loop); `canonical_bytes()` and `block_hash()` forward to the kernel's `canonical_encode` and `block_hash` reads. The field order is the sorted payload-key order, so renaming a payload key needs a `schema_version` bump (ADR-0005 § 3.1) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0005 sync; the owner `[u32 tag][u32 length][field.to_byte_array()]` layout is withdrawn)*. **`block_hash()`** is a kernel-side read, not Graph code: `block_hash(b) = H64(canonical_encode(snapshot payload of b))`, where H64 = the first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 that native `HashingContext` returns, read as a little-endian two's-complement int (ADR-0005 § 4.1 — a truncated hash, never a hand-rolled 64-bit mix); the kernel caches it per block, invalidated by the block's touch serial (every granted `open_for`), not by a dirty key (ADR-0005 § 5.2), and recomputes it at most once per kernel snapshot or `state_hash` request *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0005 sync)*. The kernel's `state_hash` fold, its framing and `hash_algo` are defined in ADR-0005 § 4.4 and are not restated here; the Graph's `canonical_bytes()` and `block_hash()` feed it unchanged. The one-level Merkle form with per-block cached hashes is the kernel's K-1, decided by ADR-0005 § 5 and not a rule of this GDD (R5). **SHARED_SUMMARY** (VS-B): per compartment `T_dC` (int16, 0.1 °C), `P` (u16), `p_o2` (u16), three bands (3 bits each); per node/edge `state` (3 bits) + `sev` (3 bits) + `served_q` (0..15); per loop component `pool_q`; active descriptors compact `(id, mode, sev, alarm_eligible, intensity bucket = intensity_pm / 100, since_steps, mode_steps, grow_steps, each saturating at 2^24 − 1)` — 7 bytes for the first six fields plus 3 bytes for each of the two GA-T ages, 13 bytes each, from which a client derives `fail_since_step` and the trail's own age so two MIRROR crewmates see equal trail extent, dullness and density (CR-10, VS-B) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from failure-and-trail-system; GA-T fields added 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; seam list; about 0.4 KB at MVP, deltas ride the dirty keys; clients never receive `t_rem`, queues or RNG inputs — they receive truth, quantised. **Interchange (S-1, decided by ADR-0006):** the Graph's snapshot payload is a Dictionary of named packed arrays; Save/Load stores it with `var_to_bytes` (lossless for int64) and the hash input is ADR-0005's TLV encoding of the same payload — never `var_to_bytes` bytes (ADR-0005 Migration item 2; no `canonical_bytes` embedding in the payload). The Graph never uses a `Resource` for saves (R6). JSON appears only in the save header and in the dev-only `dump-save`, which renders any int at or above 2^53 as a decimal string and a `PackedByteArray` as `Marshalls.raw_to_base64`; it is diagnostics, never a load path (Godot JSON parses numbers as float — TD, sourced). The Graph's own values nevertheless stay below 2^53 in practice (step numbers, counters and stocks are bounded by D.13), but the save form does not depend on that *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync; replaces the "values < 2^53, base64 in any JSON text, no `var_to_bytes`" form of S-1)*. Restore is two-phase (decode and validate into a scratch state, then copy the contents into the existing block object); `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` supports exactly version 1 in MVP, and every failure is reported through `ctx.fault(GRAPH_RESTORE_*)` with the Graph's domain code and a named detail, never by return value and never by clamping, with the live state untouched (Section E) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync, § 2.2; TR-lsg-023)*. Type ids are append-only forever — the only forward-compatibility promise v1 makes.

**LS-22 — Falsifiability: perception-agnostic by construction.** No mutator argument carries a believed state; every argument is an id or a physical magnitude; the Graph never reads `PERCEPTION_OUT` (kernel CR-12) and `read_view` returns true values only, so a hallucinated "fixed" pipe (the Filter shows OK while `hp` = 2000) cannot change a Graph value and a hallucinated repair performs the real `repair_step` increments against the true `hp` — it costs time, not truth. Every gauge quantity has **one physical witness driven by the same Graph value**, so a lying instrument can be falsified by the world:

**LS-14 — `FailureDescriptor` schema.** Derived each run in phase 11 from state (only `fail_since_step`, `warn_since_step` and the three GA-T onset fields `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` and `isolated_at_step` are persisted *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); the Graph emits semantics, never visuals.

------
**LS-15 — Seams: a weld moves nothing.** Sections are instantiated into the one world graph when they exist (`instantiate_section`); ids come from the block's `next_*` counters in template order, so a weld **only adds edges** and never renumbers. A weld plan is plain data `{ section_a, section_b, pairs[]: (node_a, port_a, node_b, port_b, loop), openings[]: (comp_a, comp_b, area_max), L_seam, q }` validated by the pure query `can_join(plan)` with the closed reason set `SECTION_UNKNOWN`, `SECTION_NOT_LOADED` (dormant counts as not loaded), `SOCKET_OCCUPIED`, `PORT_INCOMPAT`, `PORT_ABSENT` (ABSENT, DESTROYED or SALVAGED endpoint), `SEAM_LIMIT` (> `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION` 8), `ALREADY_JOINED`, `CAPACITY` (`MAX_GRAPH_NODES` 4096 / `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` 8192), `POWER_CYCLE` (the cable pairs would close a cycle in POWER wiring — R12: islands are trees, cycles are rejected here and at data load, VS-A may lift it), `STABILITY` (D.12). It returns the fully resolved plan (slot indices, edge count) and informational `surge[]` per sub-edge (D.14), flagging an opening whose `|ΔP| > WELD_DP_WARN` 300 dkPa — **a warning, never a reject**; the warning is diegetic: the closed hatch's own `SEAL_STRAIN` descriptor (CREAK at the rim, rim frost when `|ΔT| > HATCH_DT_FROST_MC`; D.14, LS-14) and the corruptible gauge. `surge[]` reaches the player only through those tells and instruments — never as a number in a weld preview or any other UI; Assembly's preview may consume `surge[].warn` to pick a diegetic cue, not to print the value *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. `weld_join` then only appends the pre-validated edges, writes the SeamRecord, sets every sub-edge **disconnected** (R9: opening `area` 0, pipe and duct valves closed, cable breaker open), bumps `topology_version` and marks `T` + `S/<seam_id>` + `SEC/<a>` + `SEC/<b>`; nothing in it can fail, so CR-9's infallible apply holds. Connecting is then three lit verbs (`set_opening_area`, `set_valve`, `set_breaker`), each with its own surge read-out. The seam weeps through `A_seam_m` from the step it exists (D.2, D.14) until wear-in or a seam PATCH (M7; V11 SEAL_SEAM is the VS-A form) — the weld's own P1 tell. **Structural half, returns, seam read** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from modular-ship-assembly, ship-section-and-layout-data-model)*: `can_join_static(plan)` is published as a pure query returning the first failing reason of the nine structural reasons in LS-15 order — `SECTION_UNKNOWN`, `SECTION_NOT_LOADED`, `SOCKET_OCCUPIED`, `PORT_INCOMPAT`, `SEAM_LIMIT`, `ALREADY_JOINED`, `CAPACITY`, `POWER_CYCLE`, `STABILITY` — reading no node `hp`, `state`, `forced_mode` or `served_pm` and computing no `surge[]`; `can_join` adds `PORT_ABSENT` (a node-state read) at its LS-15 position and the `surge[]` read-out. `weld_join` returns `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}`; `seam_view(seam_id)` → `{state, sub_edges[{kind, id}], leak_bp, opening_ids[], cut_sides[]}` is pure *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, routed from modular-ship-assembly D54 / ASK G10)*: `cut_sides` is empty unless the seam is `CUT` with boundary RAGGED, and then holds one entry per side, `{section_id, cut_holes[{cid, a_hole}], uncapped_open_ends}`, where `cid` is the compartment carrying that side's A_CUT virtual hole (one per former opening), `a_hole` is the hole's CURRENT D.2 area (24 at `hp` 2500; 0 once a Vertical Slice plate install or repair closes it) and `uncapped_open_ends` is the count of that side's fluid ports still `open_end`. It is derived from the hull-stub records and port flags already in `graph.state` (no new persisted field; the SeamRecord tombstone keeps the cut hole ids). The Graph has no keep / leave notion: it returns BOTH sides keyed by `section_id`, and Assembly picks the keep sides from Layout's `keep_sections`. A welded section keeps its `kind` and `rate_pm` (LS-17, LS-25): M2 does not promote a DERELICT section, so a cut restores nothing. An as-welded seam is **not quiet**: it moves nothing between the sections, but it weeps (HISS at the seam) from its first run until wear-in brings `leak_bp` to 0 at period 100 or V1 patches it — the weep tapers **linearly with `leak_bp`** to a cliff at 0 (D.14), not a function of `q`. **Intended seam clock** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a default weld (`q` 850, `L_seam` 3) is tight at period 100 = 16.7 min; the weld-side bay loses about 20 % of its gas over that time if nothing compensates: its total pressure never leaves NORMAL (D.15 SEAM-WEEP), but with its vent isolated its O2 band enters THIN at about step 4,325 (7.2 min) and stays there until the vent runs or the seam is sealed — a deliberate sev-1 tell of the unvented bay, absent with the vent live; V1 PATCH on the seam ends the weep at once (M7 sets `leak_bp` to 0 on a SEAM) and a running vent makes the gas up. The weep carries no LEAK wear (D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Alternative considered:* opening the seam at weld with a hard reject above a `ΔP` limit (SD OQ-13) — rejected (R9): it created a vacuum-section soft-lock and a loop-surge leak; the disconnected start removes both and makes every connection a readable choice.

**LS-16 — Cuts, only along seams.** `cut_detach(seam_id, boundary_mode)` is atomic in one P2 apply. `SEALED` (cut at a bulkhead or hatch): the seam's OPENINGs are removed, its loop sub-edges tombstoned, both sides' fluid ports `capped` — nothing leaks. `RAGGED` (cut through the weld): for each former opening a virtual hole of `A_CUT` 24 is attached to each side's compartment as a hull stub with `hp` 2500 (sev 4 — D.4 gives sev 4 at `hp` ≤ 2500 — BREACH, exogenous — no gate) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G4)*, and each side's fluid ports become `open_end` (SEVERED) leaking at `OPEN_END_RATE_PM` (500 ‰ of port cap per step) until `cap_port`. **The two RAGGED hazards are independent** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, routed from modular-ship-assembly D54)*: `cap_port` (M12) closes a fluid port's hiss only and never changes the hull hole. The A_CUT hull stub (`hp` 2500, `a_hole` 24) has no subject in the MVP: no verb patches, caps or repairs it, so the cut room vents to its steady state, `band_p` VACUUM, and stays a vacuum until a Vertical Slice plate install closes the hole (the same "room is lost" rule as a DESTROYED hull segment). With `n` holes of area A_CUT on a room of volume `V`: `k = G_OPEN × A_CUT × n / (V × GAS_SCALE)`; the room reaches DECOMP (`P` < 400) in `ceil(ln(1000/400)/k)` steps and VACUUM (`P` < 100) in `ceil(ln(1000/100)/k)` steps, `P0` 1000 dkPa nominal. `V` 20, `n` 1: `k` = 2 × 24 / 20000 = 0.0024; DECOMP `ceil(381.8)` = 382 steps = 2,292 ticks (38 s); VACUUM `ceil(959.4)` = 960 steps = 5,760 ticks (96 s). `V` 30, `n` 1: `k` = 0.0016; VACUUM `ceil(1439.1)` = 1,440 steps = 8,640 ticks. A room open to a larger connected volume vents more slowly (`k` uses the connected volume). Guarantees: no inventory lives in edges, so removing them creates or destroys nothing; power has no inventory; the current step's exchange across the seam is simply not computed; one notification batch with `T`, `S/<seam_id>`, affected `C/<id>`; the next run re-derives components. Cutting through a compartment is not a Graph operation and is not allowed (R10): a compartment belongs to one section and a cut never splits gas by a volume ratio. `discard_section(section_id)` (jettison, Web Map unload in VS-A) tombstones a section's slots; mass in it leaves the world and is added to the counters as `discarded_*` so the invariant still closes; ids are never reused.

**LS-17 — Sections and dormancy.** Every node, edge and compartment carries `section_id`; a section record holds `kind` (HOME / DERELICT), `dormant`, `rate_pm` (LS-25), `stress_until_step`, the three conservation counters and `discarded_*`. A section is **dormant** when its derelict is not loaded (zoomed out, left behind): its slots are skipped by every phase, its atmosphere and failures stand still, its state is persisted and hashed unchanged, and it cannot be welded (`SECTION_NOT_LOADED`). The flag is written only by M19 `set_section_dormant` (Web Map & Transit at load/unload) and read through the pure `section(section_id)` → `{kind, dormant, rate_pm, stress_active}` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from web-map-and-transit)*. The section record also carries `dormant_since_step` (persisted; stamped when `dormant` is set); on load M19 also advances, by `step_no − dormant_since_step`, every subject's `mode_since_step` and non-zero `isolated_at_step` (GA-T, LS-14: a trail's age counts only the steps the section ran) **and** `warn_since_step` (while `has_warn`), `fail_since_step` (of every FAILED or DESTROYED subject) and `patched_at_step` (of every patched subject, `hp_cap` < `HP_FULL`), and every SeamRecord's `built_step` and `mode_since_step`, so the fairness gate never counts as served a warning the player never witnessed and a patch's decay clock does not run while the section sleeps; `stress_until_step` is deliberately not advanced (the breach rhythm's stress lapses while a section sleeps); then it sets `dormant_since_step` to 0 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Loading it clears `dormant` and it resumes from its last state with no fast-forward (R13; SD OQ-2 resolved: cheapest, and a derelict that "does not degrade on its own" is the boarding rhythm GD asks for). VS-A (ADR-LSG-04): on unload the partition is serialised into Web Map's deltas and the slots are compacted away by an explicit order-preserving compaction mutator; reload re-creates them with **new** ids. Quiescence sleeping of islands (D.16) is the VS-A lever on top of dormancy, with its flag persisted so a restore resumes with the same awake set.

**LS-18 — Published mutators (M1–M19), two classes.** All are callable only inside a kernel-issued `WriteScope` in P2/P3, every signature takes the scope token first, and every one marks its dirty keys explicitly (packed-array element writes run no setter). **Class A** is command-backed: paired with a pure `check_*` used by the owner command's `validate`; `apply` is infallible once the check passed. **Class B** is the unconditional channel (kernel CR-9 path (a)): never rejects, clamps, and treats an unknown or stale id as a no-op returning 0/false. The Graph registers **no commands of its own**; the domain commands live with Assembly, Interaction, Suit, Emitter State and Horror (kernel H2).
-----
**LS-24 — Invariants, FAULTED tiers, bounded work.** Two tiers, and every invariant in this GDD belongs to one. *Structural (hard):* edge endpoint slot out of range or pointing at a tombstone; array lengths disagree; ids not strictly ascending; `next_id ≤ max id`; CSR inconsistent with edges; a seam sub-edge whose SeamRecord is missing — checked after every topology mutator in debug, in `post_restore` in all builds, every run in debug; a violation is a kernel step-invariant failure → FAULTED (dev halts; release returns to the menu; no autosave). Every check is raised through `GraphFault.raise(code, subject)`, which records the code, returns the failure to the kernel and, in debug, also halts; no invariant relies on GDScript `assert`, which is stripped from release builds and cannot be caught *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Numeric (soft):* an amount below 0, a field above its documented max, conservation drift ≠ 0, `ΔT` clamped — in release clamp to range, increment `graph_saturations[field]` and continue; in debug `GraphFault.raise` halts. Every test suite asserts `graph_saturations` is all zeros, so a rounding defect still fails CI without ejecting a player from a 40-minute session. Work per run is bounded by construction (D.16): one pass per loop, `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP` failures, `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` writes, never catch-up; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` (registry 4 ms, "Diagnostic alarm for P3; target is 2 ms") is the kernel's logging threshold, not a cut-off, and the Graph's own budget of record is the **spike share** it asks of that 2 ms target — the sum of the Graph hooks that run on one hook tick at **P99 ≤ 0.5 ms and max ≤ 1.0 ms** on a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release template, `forward_plus`, vsync on, 120-frame warm-up) on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (delegated ruling R12; `project.yaml` `qa.min_spec`; pending spike measurement; pass needs P99 within the R12 headroom of the frame ceiling) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)* — with the allocation, read-side and decision-ladder clauses of D.16; the first draft's "10 ms at 10 Hz" framing was wrong, because the constraint is a spike on one 60 Hz frame in six that every other divisor-6 hook shares, and the technical-director's apportionment of the 2 ms target is Open Question 31 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.

**LS-25 — Endogenous rates: wear, compression, stress.** Everything that damages a subject without a player or a horror doing it is one of: overload (D.9) and the short burn of a FAILED cable in SHORT (D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, wear on period steps (LEAK, OVERHEAT, fatigue, patch decay, and **duty** — `W_DUTY_BP_PER_100` on every running SCRUBBER, PUMP, REACTOR and HEATER, D.9, so that a fully repaired ship is quiet for a session but never permanently safe (P5): at 2 bp per period a healthy machine reaches `HP_OK` after 1500 periods = 4.2 h of continuous duty and carries WORN from then on *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*), thaw-burst (C5). All of it is multiplied by the section's `rate_pm` (HOME 1000; DERELICT `10^6 / DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION` = 2000, so a derelict fault's wear clock runs at half length; clocks set by a stock draining — a tank emptying, a pool venting — do not compress) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* and by `stress_pm` (`BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` 2000 while the section is stressed by M17 STRESS, 1000 otherwise). The multipliers never touch gas exchange, heat conduction or supply: the breach rhythm makes the ship *fail* faster, not *leak* faster — the hole still sets the hiss. On a derelict, faults that are "dead" (dried trails) are authored as subjects at `hp` ≤ `HP_FAIL` with a `def_id` whose module is powered-off, so they emit descriptors with `intensity_pm` 0 and `since_steps` large (the dried trail) and only wake when power or coolant reaches them.

**LS-26 — The MVP slice (R23) and what waits.** *Mode count note (consistency check 2026-10-26): "six MVP modes" are six hazard groups — LEAK, SHORT/OVERLOAD, OVERHEAT/SCRAM, FREEZE, BREACH, STARVE — spanning ids 1–7 and 9; SEVERED (8) is also MVP-live by construction because salvage (V8, M6/M12) produces an `open_end`; WORN (10) and SEAL_STRAIN (26) are non-hazard and live wherever hp or a closed hatch exists.* Home-ship (handmade): 5 compartments — cryo bay, corridor, engine room, cargo bay, airlock/pod dock — with all five loops: 1 REACTOR, 1 BATTERY, 2 CABLE_JUNCTIONs with breakers, ~8 LOADs (lamps 20 W at `waste_permille` 1000, door motors, scrubber 600 W at 400 ‰, pump 400 W at 300 ‰, one HEATER 500 W at 1000 ‰ in the cryo bay — the heat budget that keeps the ship at COMFORT, D.15 HEALTHY), ~8 CABLEs; 1 SCRUBBER, 1 O2_TANK (3,000,000 mGU), 5 VENTs, ~5 DUCTs (one exposed, in the cryo bay, authored as a spur so that its FAILED state cuts no vent's `path_cap`, D.15 O2-SHIP) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; 1 RESERVOIR (20,000 mL), 1 PUMP, 1 RADIATOR, 3 PIPEs; 1 FUEL_TANK, 2 FUEL PIPEs; 7 HULL_SEGMENTs (two breachable per outer room); 1 weld socket. ~40 nodes, ~55 edges (all counts in this rule are estimates; Derelict Authoring's templates are of record, e.g. 11 home-ship LOADs) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from derelict-authoring-handmade-kits)*. Derelict A (cold wreck, first sortie — the home-ship is the spawn; registry `mvp_template_roster`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from derelict-authoring-handmade-kits, boarding-and-salvage)*: 4 compartments, dead bus, 1 BATTERY at partial charge, scrubber FAILED (`hp` 2000) to salvage (first V8), one frozen and leaking PIPE, 4 segments; ~30 nodes. Derelict B (hot wreck, second sortie, the weld donor): 5 compartments, live REACTOR in SCRAM, one latent seam fault, a hull breach, coolant leak behind the overheat; ~35 nodes. ≤ 12 compartments at the weld (this bounds the welded body, home + B = 10, not the loaded set {home + B, A} = 14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from derelict-authoring-handmade-kits, modular-ship-assembly)*. The eight faults, each on a D.15 fixture: O2 pinhole at a clamp (exposed DUCT LEAK — the ship clock), O2 seam leak after weld (`A_seam_m` — the room clock, D.15 SEAM-WEEP), bus overload (PWR-OVL), broken breaker (a CABLE_JUNCTION at `hp` 2000, branch dark until replaced, D.15 BROKEN-BREAKER), coolant leak (CLT-LEAK), pump stall (PUMP STARVE on a dead branch → C3, D.15 PUMP-STALL), fuel flange drip (FUEL-DRIP) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, hull fatigue → breach (HULL-FATIGUE). Verbs: V1 patch, V3 breaker, V4 bulkhead, V5 valve, V6 emergency vent, V8 salvage, V9 weld, V12 hand crank = M11 `reset_node` only, LS-18 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, **V7 top-up** — **an MVP verb by user ruling (D34, D40, D70b, X5, 2026-10-27)**: a deliberate, actively chosen O2 tap at a lit port, which reaches the Graph as a Suit-side M16 `withdraw_store` call at the tank port (the Graph's M16 was MVP-live already and gains no rule); Suit runs `TOPUP_MODE` VERB with `CELL_ENABLED` on, so the lamp cell and the Pillar 3 "go dark" lever exist at MVP; Open Question 20 is resolved *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; modes live: LEAK, SHORT/OVERLOAD, OVERHEAT/SCRAM, FREEZE, BREACH, STARVE (plus WORN on every duty-worn machine and SEAL_STRAIN at the closed seam hatch — both live in MVP by construction, neither a hazard mode; *Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN*). The first fault the player meets is a coolant frost trail from the cryo bay (a coolant PIPE LEAK in a cryo bay authored at `T` −2000 mC, FROST band, so the drip frosts — the art bible's carried element). MVP must prove: C2/C3/C6 readable from the world; one weld joining a derelict (power + air + opening) with physical consequences (weep at the seam, draught when the hatch opens); save v1 round-trip with `state_hash`; the six modes live. **Waits for VS-A:** fire and C9, C10 and STRUT load, HEAT_EXCHANGER, FRAME_NODE, FUEL_PORT, CO2, V2/V10/V11, procedural subgraph templates, multiple reservoirs, footprint kinds beyond the five, quiescence sleeping, compaction and Web Map deltas, the hook stagger, power cycles.

**D.13 Boot product-max assertion — overflow is designed out, not detected**

The `product_max_assertion` formula is defined as:

`∀ (a, b) ∈ PRODUCTS : max_a × max_b < 2^62` asserted once at boot over the table below; a violation refuses to start the build (`GRAPH_BOOT_PRODUCT_OVERFLOW(a, b)`)

Derived: three-factor products are asserted pairwise on their running maximum (`max_ab = max_a × max_b`, then `max_ab × max_c`); every field maximum is a `GraphTuning` constant and a numeric soft invariant (LS-24): in release a field exceeding its max is clamped and `graph_saturations[field]` increments; in debug it raises `GraphFault` (LS-24; never GDScript `assert`)

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| PRODUCTS | list | fixed | constant (the table below, maintained with the code) | Every multiplication the propagation path forms |
| max_x | int | documented per field | data file (`GraphTuning.max_*`) | Field maxima |
| 2^62 | int | 4.61 × 10^18 | constant | Headroom below the int64 limit (GDScript `int` wraps silently [UNV, S0-b]) |

| Product (formula) | Operands and maxima | Worst value | Headroom |
|---|---|---|---|
| `G_OPEN × A_m × abs(g)` (D.1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | 10 × 512,000 × 6 × 10^10 | 3.1 × 10^17 | 15 |
| `n_a × V_b` (D.1 gradient `g`) | 3 × 10^8 × 200 | 6.0 × 10^10 | 7.7 × 10^7 |
| `G_OPEN × A_m × n_tot_src` (D.1 exterior) | 10 × 512,000 × 3 × 10^8 | 1.5 × 10^15 | 3.1 × 10^3 |
| `Δn × n_o2_src` (D.1 split) | 3 × 10^8 × 3 × 10^8 | 9.0 × 10^16 | 51 |
| `A_SEAM_MAX × leak_bp × (1000 − q)²` (D.2) | 32 × 10^4 × 10^6 | 3.2 × 10^11 | 1.4 × 10^7 |
| `1000 × n_o2` (D.3) | 10^3 × 3 × 10^8 | 3.0 × 10^11 | 1.5 × 10^7 |
| `R_SCR × eff × sat` (D.5) | 1000 × 1000 × 1000 | 10^9 | 4.6 × 10^9 |
| `SP_IN × V × GAS_SCALE` (D.5) | 1500 × 200 × 1000 | 3.0 × 10^8 | 1.5 × 10^10 |
| `R_MAKEUP × eff × sat` (D.5) | 6000 × 1000 × 1000 | 6.0 × 10^9 | 7.7 × 10^8 |
| `K_HULL × S_ext × |ΔT|` (D.7) | 100 × 80 × 350,000 | 2.8 × 10^9 | 1.6 × 10^9 |
| `K_HOLE × Σ A_hole × |ΔT|` (D.7) | 10 × 512 × 350,000 | 1.8 × 10^9 | 2.6 × 10^9 |
| `1000 × Q_net` and `ΔT × C` (D.7) | 10^3 × 10^6 ; 5000 × 1.2 × 10^6 | 10^9 ; 6 × 10^9 | ≥ 7.7 × 10^8 |
| `K_CAP × circ × ΔT` (D.8) | 150 × 1000 × 350,000 | 5.3 × 10^10 | 8.8 × 10^7 |
| `K_RAD × eff_r × circ × ΔT` (D.8) | 150 × 1000 × 1000 × 350,000 | 5.3 × 10^13 | 8.8 × 10^4 |
| `C_COOL × level_ml` and `Δt_cool × C_COOL × level_ml` (D.8) | 8 × 10^5 ; 5000 × 8 × 10^5 | 8 × 10^5 ; 4 × 10^9 | ≥ 10^9 |
| `OVL_K × (ρ − 1000)²` (D.9) | 16 × 39,000² | 2.4 × 10^10 | 1.9 × 10^8 |
| `Δhp × rate_pm × stress_pm` (D.9) | 10,000 × 2000 × 3000 | 6 × 10^10 | 7.7 × 10^7 |
| `W_DUTY_BP_PER_100 × duty_pm` (D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* | 6 × 1000 | 6 × 10^3 | 7.7 × 10^14 |
| `G_OPEN × A_max × 10^6` (D.12) | 10 × 512 × 10^6 | 5.1 × 10^9 | 9 × 10^8 |

**Output Range:** the worst product in the system is `G_OPEN × A_m × abs(g)` at 3.1 × 10^17, a headroom of 15 below 2^62 (the corrected gas maximum is ten times the first draft's and `A_m` a thousand times its area, so the margin is thin on purpose and is exactly why the table is asserted at boot) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, and the worst thermal product is `K_RAD × eff_r × circ × ΔT` at 5.3 × 10^13, a headroom of 8.8 × 10^4 below 2^62 — so TD's two-stage temperature form and high-pressure tank caveat (both written against SI mmol/mK units) do not apply to the game units of R1, and no intermediate ever needs a divide-before-multiply. The assertion exists so that this stays true when a designer raises a maximum: a `V_max` of 20,000 tiles or a `GAS_SCALE` of 10^6 would trip it at boot rather than wrap at 2 a.m. in a playtest.
**Example:** at boot `max_K_RAD` = 150, `max_eff` = 1000, `max_circ` = 1000, `max_|ΔT|` = 350,000 → 150 × 1000 = 150,000; × 1000 = 1.5 × 10^8; × 350,000 = 5.25 × 10^13 < 4.61 × 10^18 → pass. If a mod raised `max_|ΔT|` to 10^9 mC the final product would be 1.5 × 10^17 — still a pass — but raising `GAS_SCALE` to 10^6 raises `n_max` to 3 × 10^11 and `G_OPEN × A_m × abs(g)` to 3 × 10^20, which the assertion refuses at boot (`GRAPH_BOOT_PRODUCT_OVERFLOW(G_OPEN × A_m, abs(g))`), and Section G's safe range forbids it anyway.

**Block states.** `EMPTY` (`default_state()`: no sections, counters at 1, `last_step_no` 0) → `LIVE` (after M1 or a successful restore; hooks run; mutators accept) → `RESTORING` (two-phase restore into scratch; the live block is untouched until the contents are copied in; a `GRAPH_RESTORE_*` failure is reported with `ctx.fault` and leaves the block's contents as they were before the restore, while the kernel's LOADING → FAULTED path owns the exit) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync, § 2.2)* → `FAULTED` (kernel state after a structural invariant failure in any build or a numeric `GraphFault` in debug: hooks and mutators stop, the kernel owns the exit — dev halt or release-to-menu with no autosave; the partial writes of the failing apply are left in place for the diagnostic dump). The Graph never transitions itself out of FAULTED; a new world or a restore of the last good snapshot does.

### Interactions with Other Systems

----
- **If a snapshot is restored with any of the following**, restore fails through `ctx.fault(GRAPH_RESTORE_<name>)` with the named reason as the fault detail (never a return value and never a clamp), the live block is untouched (two-phase: decode and validate into scratch, copy the contents into the block object only on success) and the kernel fires `load_failed` — never a silent default, never a partially applied world *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync, § 2.2; TR-lsg-023)*: `GRAPH_RESTORE_BAD_VERSION(stored, supported)` (anything but 1 in MVP, including 0 and `current + 1`); `GRAPH_RESTORE_BAD_TAG(tag)` (an unknown payload key, or a required key missing; the key name is the "tag" — with a Dictionary payload a duplicate key cannot exist, and a wrongly typed value is caught earlier by Save/Load's type walk) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0005/0006 sync)*; `GRAPH_RESTORE_BAD_LENGTH(field, expected, got)` (array lengths disagree or a field is truncated); `GRAPH_RESTORE_BAD_ENUM(field, slot, value)` (state, kind, mode, port type, loop or edge kind outside the type tables); `GRAPH_RESTORE_OUT_OF_RANGE(field, slot, value)` (a value 1 above its documented max — for gas `n_max(c) = P_MAX × V × GAS_SCALE` of the restored room, not a global 3 × 10^7 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* — or below 0 — a numeric *soft* violation in play is a *hard* failure on load, because a corrupt save must not be "fixed" into a different world); `GRAPH_RESTORE_ID_ORDER(slot)` (ids not strictly ascending); `GRAPH_RESTORE_QUEUE(queue, length)` (a `pending_*` queue longer than its bound, or naming an unknown compartment, node or subject) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `GRAPH_RESTORE_COUNTER(counter, max_id)` (`next_id ≤ max id`); `GRAPH_RESTORE_BAD_EDGE_ENDPOINT(edg
- **If a restore succeeds**: `post_restore` rebuilds every derived cache (components, trees, `path_cap`, degrees, `V` and `exposed_tiles` from Layout, id → slot maps) and also `served_pm` and the failure-descriptor list from the restored canonical state — the derivation parts of phases 2 and 11, which are pure functions of it, writing no persisted field and drawing no RNG — so lamps and fault glows are correct on the first presented frame, not up to `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS − 1` ticks later *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query)*; seeds the last-emitted dirty buckets from the restored values (the band and SEAL_STRAIN memory is read from the snapshot, never re-derived from the values, so the first run after a restore reproduces an uninterrupted run *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), emits exactly one `ALL`, and the next hook due runs — the power hook of step `last_step_no + 1`, or the atmo or failure hook of the step in progress when the per-hook cursors (LS-21) show it pending *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The canonical bytes immediately after restore are byte-identical to the snapshot's (tombstones included) — the S3 criterion.
- **If a save is inspected as JSON text** (the dev-only `dump-save`; JSON is never a load path, ADR-0006 § 1.2): ints at or above 2^53 appear as decimal strings and `PackedByteArray` fields as `Marshalls.raw_to_base64` strings, so a dump is readable but never fed back to `restore()`. The stored form is `var_to_bytes` of the payload Dictionary of named packed arrays; a payload whose decoded root is not a Dictionary, or that holds a forbidden type, is refused by Save/Load's type walk before `restore()` runs (constraint S-1, decided by ADR-0006) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync; replaces the JSON-text-save and base64 rule)*. The Graph's own values are all below 2^53, so the float hazard is the kernel's 64-bit counters' and the hash's, not this block's — but the decoder does not rely on that.
- **If `restore_after: [layout.state]` is not honoured** (Layout restored after the Graph): `post_restore` finds no rooms and fails with `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_ROOM` for the first compartment — loud, by design, because a compartment without a volume cannot derive a pressure. The kernel's block ordering is the fix, not a default `V`.
- **If a template's `def_id` is renamed between builds**: every save referencing it fails with `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` — pre-release saves are disposable (Save/Load SL-14: the migration obligation begins with the first build given to anyone outside the project, the three-person MVP playtest) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format)*; after release a rename needs a migration step that maps the old string, which is why `def_id` is a string and type ids are numbers.

**Content and composition**

- **If a derelict template contains a liquid pipe, a vent and a hull segment all in one 4-tile compartment with eight openings**: D.12's sum is `⌈2 × (8 × 64 + 64 + 48) × 10^6 / 4000⌉` = 312,000 ppm — accepted; the content lint also reports any compartment above 500,000 ppm as "fragile" so a later `G_OPEN` change does not surprise. Only a sixteen-door closet at `G_OPEN` 10 is refused.
- **If a template places the HEATER (500 W, `waste_permille` 1000) in a sealed 4-tile compartment** (`C` 12,000, `S_ext` 4 → 1 dJ/°C of plate loss) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the thermostat (D.7) throttles it — the closet settles where `500 × duty_t` equals its loss, just under `T_SET_MC` (about 21.8 °C), with no SCORCH and no `MAX_DT` saturation (41 mC per step at full request). The first draft's fixed heater would have climbed 500 °C above ambient in the same closet; with its door open to a corridor the 640 dJ/step per 10 °C of `K_OPEN` conduction carries the heat out and the closet sits a few degrees above the corridor. The content lint now computes `ΔT_eq` for every heated compartment from its **non-heater** sources with the doors closed and reports any above 60 °C, because a heater can no longer drive a room past `T_SET_MC`; the heater's `req_max` is a module-def cap, not a Graph clamp.
- **If a fuel puddle (`fuel_puddle_ml > 0`) sits in a compartment that goes below 0 °C**: nothing changes in MVP — the puddle descriptor stays, fire is VS-A (R8), and the Body's "slows walking" is read from `fuel_puddle_ml` whether frozen or not. VS-A may add a `frozen` presentation hint from the room band; the Graph will not add a field for it.
- **If the home-ship's cryo bay is authored at `T` −2000 mC (FROST band) so the first fault's coolant drip frosts** (LS-26): the room reads FROST from the first run with its `ATMO_COLD` sev 2 descriptor, the heater (tier 3, 500 W) warms it once powered: for a generic V 20 room (`C` 60,000 dJ/°C) at `ΔT` ≈ 500 × 1000 / 60,000 = 8 mC per step, 2.5 min to COMFORT; the authored 42-tile cryo bay (registry `room_volume`: V 42, `C` = 42 × 3000 = 126,000 dJ/°C) at ≈ 4 mC per step gross — about 5 min to COMFORT before plate loss and about 6.5 min with it (Derelict Authoring D.18) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from derelict-authoring-handmade-kits)* — and the frost trail from the leak stops growing when the band leaves FROST. The onboarding sequence is a physical one: restore power, feel the room warm, follow the drip to the clamp, patch it.
- **If Layout changes a compartment's `V` while the world runs** (not possible in MVP; a VS-A Assembly feature): the Graph re-bases the energy pair so `U = T × C + t_rem` is preserved (`T` unchanged, `t_rem` recomputed against the new `C`) and `P` changes by the volume ratio on the next derivation — the gas did not move, the room did. Recorded here so the VS-A rule is written against conservation, not against `P`.


**Build assertions on this table** (a violation refuses to boot, Section H): `HP_FAIL < LEAK_HP ≤ HP_OK`; `HP_FAIL < BREACH_HP ≤ HP_OK`; `LEAK_HP + PATCH_DECAY_BP_PER_100 ≤ PATCH_CAP_BP < HP_OK < HP_FULL`; `FREEZE_ON_MC ≥ T_AMB_MC + 10000`; `FREEZE_WARN_MC ≥ FREEZE_ON_MC + 5000`; `FREEZE_OFF_MC ≥ FREEZE_ON_MC + 5000` and `FREEZE_OFF_MC ≤ FREEZE_WARN_MC`; `L_CAV_LO < L_CAV_HI`; `SP + SP_IN ≤ P_MAX`; `T_SET_MC − T_PROP_MC > FREEZE_WARN_MC`; `OVERHEAT_SCRAM_STEPS ≥ W_MIN_STEPS`; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*  `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` = the registered divisor; `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES < 2^20`; `HP_FAIL < BURST_HP_TO < LEAK_HP` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; band boundaries monotone; the largest mode id ≤ 31 (`GRAPH_BOOT_MODE_ID`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; D.12's gas sum and thermal sum for every template compartment (`GRAPH_BOOT_STABILITY`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; `10 × Q_MIN ≥ max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP)` (`GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING`); D.13's product table.

**Registered** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from failure-and-trail-system, horror-entities, attention-system)*: `LEAK_HP`, `BREACH_HP`, `SEV_STEP`, `A_HOLE_MAX`, `ALARM_SEV_MIN`, `OPEN_END_RATE_PM`, `FOOTPRINT_MAX_Q`, `FOOTPRINT_MAX_GOUGE_BP`, `FREEZE_WARN_MC`, `FREEZE_ON_MC`, `FREEZE_OFF_MC`, `OVERHEAT_ON_MC`, `OVERHEAT_OFF_MC`, `RUPTURE_HP`, `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`, `INRUSH_PM`, `INRUSH_STEPS`, `C_TILE`, `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`, `DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION` and `GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS` are in `design/registry/entities.yaml` with this GDD as source; the rows above are their values of record. **Not yet registered (registry requests, 2026-10-27 review)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the ★ rows `SHORT_BURN_BP_PER_STEP`, `THAW_ROLL_STEPS`, `BURST_HP_TO` and `BURST_P_PM`; and three changed entries, `BATT_DIS_CAP` (registered at 2000, now 1000), `GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS` (its value text still reads "per run"; it is per hook tick) and `weld_quality` (owner Modular Ship Assembly: `Q_MIN` now covers `max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP)`). Registered since the design review and no longer open: `R_MAKEUP`, `T_SET_MC` / `T_PROP_MC`, `P_MAX`, the P-band and T-band boundaries, `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` and the milli-area form of `seam_at_weld` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

- **GIVEN** F-MVP after a RAGGED cut (tombstoned seam edges) with one crew member breathing, **WHEN** a snapshot is taken at **each of T 1,801 … 1,805** (T 1,801, 1,803 and 1,805 are non-hook ticks and T 1,802 and 1,804 are the atmo and failure hook ticks of the staggered baseline, so the sweep crosses every intermediate offset; each with a `draw_air` queued by Suit at the preceding hook tick, a pending M17 `deposit_trace` and a pending M14 `set_load_request`) and restored into a fresh kernel, and the command stream is replayed to T 3,600 against an uninterrupted control, **THEN** `state_hash(PERSIST, 3600)` is equal in all five restores, the first run after each restore applies the restored breath, trace and load change, and on a mismatch the test names the first differing payload key and slot; a negative control that leaves the queues out of the snapshot payload must fail the same test *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0005 sync)*. The renumber baseline is the Graph's code-side enum constants: the data file must equal them exactly, so a renumber needs a reviewed code change. `GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID` is a fault domain 2 (content data) code raised by the start-up content loader, while `GRAPH_RESTORE_*` codes stay in the Graph's domain 3 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — ADR-0007 sync, § 2.3 and § 3.2; ADR-LSG-08 is decided by ADR-0007)*. (auto) [LS-2, LS-3, LS-4, LS-5; R19]

(auto) [LS-4]

(auto) [D.3; LS-7 hysteresis]
- **GIVEN** each threshold of LS-7 and each hp and gate threshold, **WHEN** the value is set to N and N + 1 on either side of the boundary — `p_o2` 179 / 180, 139 / 140, 99 / 100; `P` 699 / 700, 399 / 400, 99 / 100; `T` 69,999 / 70,000, 39,999 / 40,000, 9,999 / 10,000, −1 / 0, −15,001 / −15,000; `hp` 6,999 / 7,000, 3,999 / 4,000, 3,000 / 3,001, 2,999 / 3,000; `warn_elapsed` 99 / 100; `leak_bp` 0 / 1 — and then moved back by the hysteresis margin less one and by the margin, **THEN** the band, state, `sev` or gate flips exactly on the stated side and re-enters exactly at the margin. (auto) [LS-7; D.3; D.4; D.11] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
### Serialization & restore

- **GIVEN** F-MVP at T 1,800 after S2's weld, mid-breach, **WHEN** `snapshot()` runs, **THEN** it completes in ≤ 0.5 ms (F-K ≤ 3 ms), the snapshot is ≤ 32 KB, `restore()` + `post_restore()` complete in ≤ 2 ms (F-K ≤ 10 ms), and the canonical bytes immediately after restore are byte-identical to the snapshot's, tombstones included. (spike) [LS-21; S3 cost; ADR-LSG-05]
- **GIVEN** a corpus of 1,000 mutated snapshots generated from seeds 1..1000 of F-MVP's snapshot, each **pre-classified by construction** — class V (a valid edit that must restore: a changed `hp`, an `n_o2` within `n_max(c)`), class I (an invalid edit with one expected named reason: a truncated field → `BAD_LENGTH`; an unknown or missing payload key → `BAD_TAG` *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0005/0006 sync)*; an endpoint out of range → `BAD_EDGE_ENDPOINT`; an enum out of range → `BAD_ENUM`; `stored_version` 0 and current + 1 → `BAD_VERSION`; a value 1 above its max, including `n_o2 + n_inert` 1 above `n_max(c)` → `OUT_OF_RANGE`; a queue over its bound → `QUEUE`; ids out of order → `ID_ORDER`; a counter below the max id → `COUNTER`), and class B (a single bit flip in a numeric payload, whose outcome must be either a restore or exactly one reason from the closed set and nothing else) — **WHEN** each is restored, **THEN** every V restores and hashes to its expected value, every I fails with exactly its expected reason, every B ends in one of the two allowed outcomes, the live block is byte-identical before and after every failure, and zero script errors escape; the corpus is regenerated by seed, never edited by hand, and the test prints the class counts. (auto, slow) [LS-21; Edge Cases "restore of a corrupt snapshot"; S3 corruption] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **GIVEN** a restore with Layout not yet restored, **WHEN** `post_restore` runs, **THEN** it fails with `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_ROOM`; **GIVEN** a save whose `def_id` is unknown to the Item DB, **THEN** `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF(def_id)`. (auto) [LS-21; LS-6]
- **GIVEN** a synthetic v1 → v2 migration adding one field with a default, **WHEN** the retained v1 golden save in `tests/` is restored by a v2 build, **THEN** it round-trips and its post-migration hash equals the golden v2 hash. (auto) [LS-21; S3 migration]
- **GIVEN** the persisted-field list of LS-21, **WHEN** the snapshot payload (the input to `canonical_bytes()`) is diffed against the fields the next run reads, **THEN** every field the run depends on is in the snapshot (`t_rem`, `tc_rem`, `fuel_rem`, `out_w`, `forced_mode_next`, `warn_since_step` and `has_warn`, `thaw_until_step`, `mode_since_step`, `mode_key`, `isolated_at_step`, `dormant`, `dormant_since_step`, the section counters, `def_table`, the per-hook step cursor, the three `pending_*` queues, the band, `p_prev` and SEAL_STRAIN memory, the compartment warn trackers `warn_since_o2/p/t` and `warn_bits` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*) and no derived cache is. **Method A (reflection):** the test enumerates every member of `GraphState` by reflection and fails if one is neither written into the `snapshot()` payload nor on the checked-in DERIVED allowlist (the non-persisted caches of LS-21). **Method B (zero and diff):** for each DERIVED-allowlist field the test zeroes it in a copy of a mid-fault state, runs one step, and asserts the copy's `state_hash` equals the unmodified control's — a step that reads a cache it did not first recompute shows as a differing hash, which is the mechanism for "a field the next run reads is missing from the snapshot". Both run; either failing fails the criterion. (auto) [LS-21] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings; re-review, disagreement settled per G2)*
- **GIVEN** a LEAK pipe on F-MVP whose `sev` rises 2 → 3 at step N and whose upstream valve is closed at step N + 80 and reopened at step N + 380 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings; GA-T, user ruling D30)*, **WHEN** the descriptor is read on steps N − 1, N, N + 79, N + 80, N + 200, N + 379, N + 380 and N + 381, **THEN** `mode_steps` reads (the previous mode's age), 0, 79, 80, 200, 379, 380, 381 and `grow_steps` reads (the previous mode's age), 0, 79, 80, 80, 80, 380, 381 exactly; `grow_steps` is never negative; `warn_since_step` is unchanged by the restamp at step N and by the isolation, so `since_steps` and `warn_elapsed` keep counting from it (the fairness gate reads `warn_since_step` only). A snapshot of a subject at `sev` 0 restores `mode_key` 0 and `mode_since_step` 0. (auto) [LS-14 GA-T; LS-21] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
- **GIVEN** a derelict section dormant for 3,000 steps with a LEAK of `mode_steps` 400 and an isolated descriptor of `grow_steps` 100, **WHEN** M19 resumes it, **THEN** `mode_steps` reads 400 and `grow_steps` 100 on the first run after resume (the dormant 3,000 steps are not counted), `dormant_since_step` is 0, `warn_since_step`, `fail_since_step` and `patched_at_step` have each been advanced by 3,000, `warn_elapsed` and `since_steps` read the values they had at the unload and a fairness gate that was closed at the unload is still closed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; **GIVEN** a SEAM weep, **THEN** its `mode_steps` on its first run is `step_no − built_step`. (auto) [LS-17; LS-14 GA-T] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
- **GIVEN** a snapshot of F-MVP at T 1,800 with GA-T's three per-subject fields added (9 bytes per node or edge: two int32 and one u8; about 250 subjects across home-ship, derelict A and derelict B, about 2.3 KB; plus the int32 `thaw_until_step`, 13 bytes in all, about 3.3 KB *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), **WHEN** `snapshot()` runs, **THEN** the ≤ 32 KB budget above still holds. (auto) [LS-21; GA-T] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

(auto) [LS-9] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings; re-review)*
- **GIVEN** the cryo bay (`V` 42) at 1000 dkPa (`n_o2` 8,820,000, `n_inert` 33,180,000, total 4.2 × 10^7 mGU), **WHEN** a snapshot is taken and restored, **THEN** the restore succeeds, `graph_saturations` is all zeros and no gas is clamped; **GIVEN** the same room with `n_o2 + n_inert` = `n_max(c)` + 1 = 63,000,001, **THEN** restore fails with `GRAPH_RESTORE_OUT_OF_RANGE` and a live run clamps it with one `graph_saturations` increment. (auto) [D.1; D.3; D.13; LS-24; Edge Cases "restore"] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

(auto) [LS-21; D.3; D.14] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

- **GIVEN** the Save/Load GDD (now written), **WHEN** a lint scans `design/gdd/save-load-and-versioned-format.md` for the tokens `S-1` and `K-1`, **THEN** it carries constraint S-1 as ADR-0006 decides it (payload Dictionary of named packed arrays stored with `var_to_bytes`; never as hash input; no `Resource`; JSON only in the header and dev dump, with `Marshalls.raw_to_base64` for byte blobs there) and the kernel's K-1 and D.10 notes appear in its Open Questions as routed amendments, not as Graph rules. (lint over the GDD) [LS-21; R5, R6] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; ADR-0005/0006 sync 2026-10-29)*

# Architecture Decision Registry
#
# PURPOSE: Single source of truth for key architectural stances that all ADRs
# must agree on. Skills check this before writing new ADRs to detect conflicts
# at authoring time — before stories are created against contradictory decisions.
#
# RULES:
#   - Register a stance when it constrains how OTHER systems must be built.
#     An internal implementation detail that affects only one ADR does not need
#     to be registered.
#   - Never delete entries — set status: "superseded_by: ADR-NNNN" instead,
#     quoted: unquoted, the second colon makes the file invalid YAML.
#   - When a stance changes: update the entry, set revised: to today's date,
#     add a comment with the old value, and run /architecture-review to check
#     what ADRs are now invalidated.
#   - adr: is the authoritative source. All other ADRs that depend on this

content.content:
## Summary
About fifteen systems register state blocks, step hooks and command handlers with the kernel, and the kernel must call them, check that they finished, and let them write only inside a kernel-issued scope. This ADR fixes that contract in GDScript: owners are plain objects that register typed `Callable`s (no base class), every kernel call receives a reused context and ends in `return ctx.complete()`, all writes and dirty marks go through a reused `WriteScope` (including during new-game construction), faults are integers with static per-system domains, hooks run from a precomputed schedule, and the kernel state machine is a data table that generates its own test.

## Decision

### 1. Owners register `Callable`s; owners override nothing

An owner is any object (normally a `RefCounted`) that, during `BOOTING`, passes the kernel descriptors containing `Callable`s bound to its methods. There is no `BlockOwner` base class and nothing is overridden. Each owner method the kernel calls is declared `-> CompletionToken` and its last statement is `return ctx.complete()`.

The 4.7 typed-return override rule applies only to overrides, so it does not touch owner methods. The context classes of § 3 add methods to their base and **override none**; a Guideline forbids overriding a context method, because an override of `complete() -> CompletionToken` would fall under the rule. This also avoids `@abstract` (documented since 4.5, not needed) and lets tests register a plain stub. **Every override of a typed-return owner callable returns on all paths** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07)*: a stub or subclass that overrides an owner callable inherits `-> CompletionToken` (4.7 rule) and must end every branch in `return ctx.complete()`; an early `return` without it is an `INCOMPLETE`, and a path that falls off the end is a parse error or an `INCOMPLETE` by Verification 1. That GDScript rejects at parse time a typed function with a path that has no `return` is UNVERIFIED (Verification 1); whatever it shows, the token check (§ 3) is what catches a function that aborts at run time. At registration the kernel checks every `Callable` with `is_valid()` and, where available, `get_argument_count()` against the expected arity, so a wrong signature fails boot naming the registration rather than appearing later as `INCOMPLETE`.

### 2. A block is a `RefCounted` held by its owner; the kernel holds descriptors

The kernel never stores or inspects block data. It stores descriptors and calls the owner's callables. The owner's block object is a `RefCounted` with typed fields (packed arrays for struct-of-arrays state), never a `Resource` or `Node`. **`restore` copies into the existing block object and never replaces it**, because read views are long-lived facades over that object (§ 7); a test restores a block and checks its facade sees the restored values.

**Snapshot payload contract** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07; ADR-0005 § 5.3, ADR-0006)*: every packed array an owner puts in a `snapshot` payload is a **duplicate** (`PackedXArray.duplicate()` or a freshly built array), never a live reference to the block's own array. The kernel reads the payload after `snapshot` returns, hashes it outside SAVING (ADR-0005) and may hold it while the owner keeps writing; a live reference would let a later mutator change a payload already encoded or queued for the writer. `restore` likewise copies out of `data` and keeps no reference into it. A test mutates the block after `snapshot` and checks the payload unchanged.

Every field is mandatory unless marked optional; a missing field fails boot naming the descriptor (CR-6: no silent defaults). GDScript reserves `class` as a keyword, so the GDD's `class` field is `block_class` in code.

**`BlockDescriptor`**

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `block_id` | `StringName` | Unique, namespaced (e.g. `&"graph.state"`) |
| `owner_name` | `StringName` | Registering system, for diagnostics |
| `schema_version` | `int` | Bumped on any serialised-shape change |
| `supported_versions` | `PackedInt32Array` | Versions `restore` accepts |
| `block_class` | `int` enum `SIM` / `PERCEPTION_OUT` | CR-12 |
| `persist` | `bool` | false = derived, rebuilt after load |
| `persist_scope` | `int` enum `WORLD` / `PROFILE` | Required when `persist` |
| `scope` | `int` enum `SHARED` / `PER_PLAYER` | PER_PLAYER keyed by PlayerId |
| `gameplay` | `bool` | The paused-write test (CR-16) |
| `interpolated` | `bool` | Kernel runs `commit_baseline` at P4 |
| `repl_hint` | `int` enum `HOST_ONLY` / `SHARED_SUMMARY` / `OWNER_PRIVATE` | Unused until VS-B, mandatory now |
| `restore_after` | `Array[StringName]` | DAG for ADR-0016 |
| `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state`, `post_restore`, `read_view`, `empty_view` | `Callable` | Mandatory |
| `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` | `Callable` | Mandatory iff `interpolated` |
| `init_world`, `binding_source` | `Callable` | Optional (the binding source is this field only, never a separate registration) |

**`CommandTypeDescriptor`** (complete; ADR-0002 owns the meaning of each field)

| Field | Type |
|---|---|
| `type` | `StringName` |
| `owner_name` | `StringName` |
| `allowed_origins` | `int` bitmask (`ORIGIN_PLAYER = 1`, `ORIGIN_SYSTEM = 2`) |
| `actor_binding` | `int` enum `NONE` / `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` |
| `actor_source` | `StringName` (block id; empty iff `NONE`) |
| `coalesce` | `int` enum `NONE` / `LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK` |
| `max_age_ticks` | `int` |
| `allowed_when_paused` | `bool` |
| `writes_blocks` | `Array[StringName]` |
| `payload_schema` | `Dictionary` (authoring form; compiled at registration, ADR-0002 § 3) |
| `validate`, `apply` | `Callable` |

**`HookDescriptor`**: `hook_id: StringName`, `owner_name: StringName`, `divisor: int` (≥ 1), `offset: int` (0 ≤ offset < divisor), `after: Array[Dictionary]` each `{&"id": StringName, &"tolerates_stale": bool}`, `callable: Callable`.

**`DiagnosticsChannelDescriptor`** (CR-6 via the Debug Overlay's E-DO-38): the field list is ADR-0031's; registration is here.

**Entity ids are block-local** *(GDD command-simulation-layer CR-8, TR-cmd-015)*: an entity id is allocated by the owning block's own counter and is unique only within that block; the kernel allocates no entity ids. A reference across blocks is the pair `(block_id, entity_id)`, and `(source block_id, entity_id)` is the key form used by the binding sources (ADR-0002 § 4, binding table). A block's counter lives inside the block and is part of its snapshot payload, so a restore returns it to the saved value.

### 4. `WriteScope`: reused, the only way to write and to mark dirty

```gdscript
class_name WriteScope extends RefCounted
enum Phase { CLOSED, APPLY, HOOK, PAUSED_APPLY, INIT, RESTORE }
var phase: Phase
var faulted: bool                                   # set by fault(); closes the scope (fail-closed)
func open_for(block_id: StringName) -> bool         # see the table below
func mark_dirty(block_id: StringName, key: int) -> void   # key layout: ADR-0004 § 3
func emit_event(block_id: StringName, kind: int, a0: int = 0, a1: int = 0, a2: int = 0, a3: int = 0, a4: int = 0, a5: int = 0) -> void   # P5 event record; ADR-0004 § 5
func has_opened(block_index: int) -> bool           # true from the first granted open_for of that block until the scope is re-armed (ADR-0005 § 5.3)
func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void
```

The kernel allocates the scope objects once and re-arms them (phase, writable set, `faulted = false`, dirty buffer) per use, like the contexts.

| Phase | When | `open_for(block)` true for |
|---|---|---|
| `APPLY` | P2 `apply` of one command (`RUNNING`) | any block (cross-block applies call other owners' published mutators) |
| `PAUSED_APPLY` | the paused service cycle | only blocks in the command type's `writes_blocks` (GDD CR-16) |
| `HOOK` | one P3 hook run | any block |
| `INIT` | new-game construction in `LOADING`: all `init_world` steps share one `INIT` scope, before `post_restore` (CR-18) | any block |
| `RESTORE` | an owner's `restore` / `post_restore` that uses its own mutators | the restoring block only |
| `CLOSED` | everything else, and after the first `fault` | nothing |

`init_world` therefore receives the scope: `init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext)`, and Web Map's `init_world` passes it to Layout `build_section`, Emitter `instantiate_section_emitters` and Interaction `sync_section` (architecture § Initialisation order step 6). **Dirty keys marked in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes are discarded**: on the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch per block instead (the GDD's "one ALL then silence"), which is what the PROJECTOR needs after a new game or a load; ADR-0004 defines that delivery.

`open_for` returning false writes nothing, counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-9) — except when the scope is closed because of an earlier fault, which is not counted again. Dirty keys are marked **only** through `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator that changed the data, never from a setter. The debug-build check that catches a missed mark is ADR-0004 § 7 (it compares a block's hash with the kernel's `touch_serial` and with whether any key was marked, for blocks that do not declare `quiet_writes_allowed`); this ADR no longer states the rule. `emit_event` follows the same scope rules as `mark_dirty`: it needs an open block and its records are discarded in `INIT`, `RESTORE` and `CLOSED` (ADR-0004 § 5). `has_opened` is a pure read used by the kernel's hash path (ADR-0005 § 5.3): it never opens anything and never counts a violation. `writes_blocks` is enforced in `PAUSED_APPLY` as the GDD requires; under `STRICT_DEBUG` it is also checked during `RUNNING`, where a write to a block outside `writes_blocks` is a `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED` violation, to catch undeclared cross-block writes early.

### 5. Mutators: status returns, fail-closed, no rollback

**Status values**: `OK = 0`; `REFUSED = 1` (the scope was not open for this block: a counted violation, **not** a fault, and never escalated by the caller); a **negative** value is `-fault_code` (a defect the mutator detected; it has also called `scope.fault`).

- **Class A** (validate-then-apply): a pure `check_*(views, args) -> StringName` (`&""` = OK) takes read views only; the matching mutator `name(scope, args, out) -> int` is infallible once its check passed. A mutator that produces data (a new id, a `{seam_id, opening_ids}` record) writes it into a **caller-owned `out` object** passed in, so the return value is always the status. Example: `weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int`.
- **Class B** (clamp, never reject): `name(scope, args) -> void`; it clamps out-of-range input and no-ops on a stale id; it still begins with `scope.open_for`.

**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3). **Fail-closed never depends on an engine error aborting the callee** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review)*: a release build may log a script error and continue. It is carried by the explicit paths only — mutator status checks, `scope.fault` and the closed scope — with the `STRICT_DEBUG` checks and ADR-0004's debug-build missed-mark hash as backstops. An engine error that a release build swallows and that no mutator detects is outside what the kernel can see; KRN-CTX-06 documents it rather than claims it.

**Caller procedure.** After every Class A call the caller checks the status. On `REFUSED` or a negative status it returns `ctx.complete()` at once: no further mutator calls and no second `ctx.fault` (the scope fault already counts). The kernel reads `ctx.faulted` after the callable returns.

**No rollback.** A fault leaves the blocks touched so far half-applied. This is acceptable because `FAULTED` is terminal until an explicit reload or new game (both rebuild every `WORLD` block) and the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save in `FAULTED` (GDD). Nothing here rules out OQ-15's alternative for the weld: ADR-0021 may snapshot the touched blocks before its apply and restore them on a fault, using the `snapshot` / `restore` callables this ADR defines.

### 6. Fault codes: static domains, pre-packed constants

A fault code is a positive `int`: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, `local` in `1..65535`. **Domain ids are static**, so a code means the same thing in every build, log and fixture. Each system's `*_faults.gd` (a `class_name XFaults extends RefCounted` holding only constants, never instantiated, one class per file) declares `const DOMAIN_ID` and its codes **already packed** (`const NOT_IN_SCOPE: int = (DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1`), plus `const NAMES: Array[StringName]` indexed by local code. It registers with `register_fault_domain(XFaults.DOMAIN_ID, owner_name, XFaults.NAMES)`; a duplicate or out-of-range id fails boot. A unit test checks each file's constants and `NAMES` agree. Codes are append-only and never reused. The kernel prints a fault as `domain.NAME`.

**Domain table** (static; new systems take the next free id; ids 32 and up are reserved for VS and later)

| Id | Domain | Id | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | kernel | 8 | interaction |
| 1 | save_load | 9 | suit |
| 2 | content data (item DB, templates, tuning) | 10 | assembly |
| 3 | graph | 11 | web_transit |
| 4 | layout | 12 | attention |
| 5 | body | 13 | horror |
| 6 | emitter | 14 | sanity |
| 7 | controller | 15–31 | presentation and tooling (read-view faults are diagnostics only) |

**Kernel fault codes (domain 0, closed)**

| Local | Name | Raised when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `INCOMPLETE` | a kernel-invoked callable did not return the armed token |
| 2 | `NO_OUTCOME` | `validate` called neither `ok()` nor `reject()` |
| 3 | `BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT` | the `LOADING` binding rebuild found a conflict or a binding-source fault |
| 4 | `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` | a restore payload names an unregistered block |
| 5 | `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` | a payload was saved at another `TICK_RATE` |
| 6 | `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` | the supplied `restore_epoch` is out of range |
| 7 | `CAPTURE_ERROR` | a `SAVING` capture failed |
| 8 | `DUPLICATE_ID` | boot: duplicate block, command, hook, domain or channel id |
| 9 | `HOOK_CYCLE` | boot: a cycle in hook `after` edges |
| 10 | `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY` | boot: unknown `after` hook, `restore_after` block or `writes_blocks` block, or a subscription to an unknown block (ADR-0004 § 2) |
| 11 | `ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID` | boot: a command type's `actor_source` rule fails (CR-6) |
| 12 | `COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN` | boot: a coalescing type allows both origins |
| 13 | `DESCRIPTOR_FIELD_MISSING` | boot: a mandatory descriptor field is absent |
| 14 | `SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TOO_LONG` | boot: `lcm` of divisors exceeds `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` |
| 15 | `HOOK_OFFSET_INVALID` | boot: `divisor < 1` or `offset` not in `0..divisor-1` |
| 16 | `CALLABLE_SIGNATURE` | boot: a `Callable` is invalid or has the wrong arity |
| 17 | `MEMORY_BUDGET` | boot: the CR-17 joint memory assertion fails |

A P3 above `STEP_BUDGET_MS` is a **diagnostic** (it logs the slowest hooks), not a fault.

**Violations** are counted diagnostics, not fault codes, and never change kernel state unless the GDD says so. Closed set: `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`, `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`, `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE`, `CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`, `CONTEXT_REENTRY`, `SUBMIT_DURING_SAVING`, `HANDLE_UNREGISTERED`, `RESULT_HANDLER_DEAD`, `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`, `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT`, `KNOB_REFUSED`, `BINDING_DRIFT`, `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED`, `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` (a boot warning), and, added 2026-10-28 and classified as ADR-0004 §§ 2, 3, 5 and 7 define them, `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` (a subscribe-time refusal, including the `PERCEPTION_OUT` rule of check 6), `DIRTY_KEY_INVALID`, `DIRTY_KEY_KIND_UNDECLARED`, `EVENT_OVERFLOW` and `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK` (dev, playtest and test builds only). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` each also calls `violation_handler(code, detail)`.

Each owner's local code list is written with its system ADR (ADR-0011 onward); its domain id is fixed now.

### 7. Read views: long-lived facades, issued by facet

The kernel never hands out a live container. **Each owner's `read_view(ctx)` is called once, at the registry freeze**, and delivers a long-lived getter-only facade over its block object (typed scalar getters and caller-owned-buffer queries, so hot paths allocate nothing). Each owner also supplies **`empty_view(ctx)`**: a facade of the same class whose getters return neutral values (zero, false, empty) and whose `is_empty()` is true. This replaces the GDD's per-request `read_view` (§ GDD sync); it is valid only because `restore` copies into the existing block object (§ 2).
