# ADR-0011: Life-Support Graph Data Model

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-29

## Last Verified
2026-10-29 (against `design/gdd/life-support-graph.md` LS-1 to LS-6, LS-14 to LS-21, LS-24, D.10, D.13 and Section E; ADR-0003 to ADR-0007 and ADR-0010, all Proposed; Godot 4.7.2 probes of 2026-10-29 on the editor binary, recorded in Engine Compatibility)

## Decision Makers
Claude (author), running under modes.automation: autonomous (project.yaml); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR.

## Summary
The Life-Support Graph is the largest simulation block (up to `MAX_GRAPH_NODES` nodes and `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` edges) and its determinism, save format, hash, dirty keys and read API all depend on how its state is laid out in memory. This ADR fixes that layout: one `graph.state` block held as a struct of dense packed arrays in seven tables plus a def-name CSR pair and a scalar header, with fixed-point integer units and a documented column width per field; append-only ids, slots and type enums that are never renumbered or reused; a hard split of every member into PERSISTED, DERIVED, SCRATCH or DIAGNOSTIC (reflection-checked); the snapshot, restore and fault shapes; the read-view and descriptor-store layout; the dirty-key kinds and packing; and the shared value types (`JoinPlan`, `WeldResult`, `FailureFilter`, `FailureSlice`) that ADR-0012 and ADR-0021 build on.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable, mono build probed), GDScript |
| **Domain** | Core (simulation state layout, integer arithmetic, serialization shape) |
| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM-HIGH. Everything this ADR uses predates 4.4 except typed `Dictionary[K, V]` (4.4), `@abstract` (4.5) and the two 4.7 GDScript rows in `breaking-changes.md`. The engine reference has no core or scripting module (`modules/` holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui only), so packed-array semantics, integer behaviour and reflection are sourced from ADR-0005's probe table (P1 to P22) and from this ADR's own probes, and stay UNVERIFIED on a release export until spikes S0-a and S3 run there. |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`; `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows; 4.4 to 4.5 `duplicate_deep` row); `deprecated-apis.md` (untyped Array/Dictionary pattern; `duplicate()` for nested data replaced by `duplicate_deep()` since 4.5); `current-best-practices.md` (GDScript 4.7: typed-return override, packed-array element writes); ADR-0005 Engine Compatibility P1, P5, P7, P8, P9, P11, P12, P14, P17, P20, P22 (cited by number below). No `modules/*.md` applies. |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None from 4.5 to 4.7 in the layout itself. `@abstract` (4.5) appears only on the `RoomSource` port (ADR-0010 § 3). Typed `Dictionary[int, int]` (4.4) appears in derived lookup caches only, never in a payload. The two 4.7 rows that bind this ADR: **(1)** "Packed array element writes no longer call the setter" (`breaking-changes.md`, `current-best-practices.md`): the Graph has no packed-array setters and marks every dirty key explicitly through `scope.mark_dirty` (§ 10); probed again below (P-d). **(2)** "Overrides inherit a typed return": binds anything that overrides a typed owner callable or an `@abstract` port method, so `RoomSource` implementers return on all paths (Implementation Guidelines). |
| **Verification Required** | Probed 2026-10-29 on `Godot_v4.7.2-stable_mono_win64_console.exe --headless --script` (editor binary, not a release export; scripts in `C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/adr-probes/0011/`): **(a)** the typed numeric builtins `mini`, `maxi`, `clampi`, `absi`, `signi` exist and return `int` for `int` arguments (3, 5, 5, 4, -1); **(b)** `get_property_list()` on a `RefCounted` subclass lists every script variable, underscore-prefixed ones included and in declaration order, selectable with `PROPERTY_USAGE_SCRIPT_VARIABLE` (the basis of the reflection test in § 6.3); **(c)** swapping two `PackedInt64Array` members by reference works and an alias taken before a member element write sees the write (ADR-0005 P7 reproduced); **(d)** `arr[i] = v` on a packed member runs no setter (P8 reproduced, and no setter is declared); **(e)** `PackedInt64Array.fill(0)` on 4096 elements costs 1.65 microseconds, `duplicate()` of 4096 elements 0.11 microseconds, and `duplicate()` followed by the first element write on 8192 `int32` elements 0.71 microseconds (`duplicate()` shares the buffer until the first write on either side; the copy is paid by the next mutator's first write, § Performance); **(f)** a typed `Dictionary[int, int]` answers `get(k, -1)`; **(g)** `PackedInt32Array` stores wrap to 32 bits (`3000000000` reads `-1294967296`, ADR-0005 P9) and `PackedByteArray` to 8 bits (`300` reads `44`); **(h)** `var_to_bytes` returns a `StringName` dictionary key as a `StringName` (type 21) and a `String` key as a `String` (type 4), which is why payload keys must be `String` (ADR-0006 § 1.2 walk rejects `StringName`); **(i)** a synthetic zero-filled payload with this ADR's columns measures 29,674 canonical TLV bytes (29,560 `var_to_bytes` bytes) for 105 nodes, 150 edges, 270 ports, 14 compartments, 1 seam, 3 sections and 2 queued entries per queue, and 33,144 bytes at 120 nodes and 172 edges (value-independent, so a real save differs by at most the key-text length). **Still open and named:** S0-a and S0-b on a `template_release` export (Windows, Linux x86-64, Linux arm64 / Deck) for items (c), (d), (e) and (g); S1 (SP-ENG-1) for GDScript accessor, `Callable.call` and `IntMath.floor_div` cost in the real phases; S3 (snapshot, restore and `post_restore` time and size on the F-MVP fixture on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK); LINT-SPIKE-1 for loading every Key Interfaces snippet under the ADR-0010 § 5.1 warning configuration (the snippets here follow its typing rules but have not been load-checked). |

## ADR Dependencies

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Depends On** | ADR-0003 (block descriptor, `WriteScope`, mutator status, fault domains, read-view facades; Proposed), ADR-0004 (dirty-key layout, `KeySpaceDescriptor`, quiet writes; Proposed), ADR-0005 (integer-only contract, `IntMath`, canonical encoding, sorted keys, cached hashes; Proposed), ADR-0006 (payload form, restore contract, `ctx.fault`; Proposed), ADR-0007 (type tables, `GraphTuning` as a `ScalarTable`, boot tiers, ledgers; Proposed), ADR-0010 (source layout, typing, lints; Proposed). Indirectly ADR-0001 (`ClockView.tick()` is the time source of `step_no()`) and ADR-0002 (the Graph registers no command). None is Accepted, so this ADR cannot be Accepted before them. |
| **Enables** | ADR-0012 (propagation: consumes the tables, scratch class, descriptor store and value types defined here), ADR-0013 (id split and `graph_ref_base`), ADR-0016 (restore order and `post_restore` sequence), ADR-0017 (typed getters for `served_pm`, `run_pm`, `state`), ADR-0021 (`weld_join`, `install_module` and `cut_detach` transaction), ADR-0022 and ADR-0023 (M17/M18 callers), ADR-0024 (`true_value` kinds), ADR-0026 (`set_section_dormant`), ADR-0027 (M15/M16), ADR-0028 (`served_pm` for the ambient mean). |
| **Blocks** | The Graph epic and every story that reads or writes `graph.state`; Item DB install, salvage and reinstall stories (TR-itemdb-016/031/040); the Instruments `load` reading (TR-instr-027); the Graph golden-hash and goldens-fixture stories (TR-lsg-031). Stories citing this ADR stay Blocked while it is Proposed. |
| **Ordering Note** | Write the shared pure files (`src/shared/graph/`: `GraphIds`, `GraphSchema`, `GraphLimits`, `graph_rules.gd`, `graph_products.gd`) and the `GraphTuning` freeze first, because ADR-0007's stage 1 loader and the Item DB (stage 2) call them before any kernel exists. The three ADR-0010 lint rules this ADR asks for (field-writer files, ARCH-06 exemption, owned-constant token list) should land with the first Graph file, not after. |

## Context

### Problem Statement

The Graph GDD (LS-1) fixes the contract in prose: one persisted SIM block, struct-of-arrays, zero floats, store extensive and derive intensive, exact conservation, ascending-slot iteration, no Dictionary on the sim path, append-only ids. It defers eleven implementation questions to an ADR, of which this one takes three (ADR-LSG-01 struct-of-arrays layout, ADR-LSG-02 the fixed-point unit system, ADR-LSG-04 append-only topology identity). Meanwhile the Foundation ADRs have since made decisions the GDD could not know, and some of them change the GDD's wording: the payload is a plain Dictionary encoded by the kernel (ADR-0005 § 3.1), payload keys and values are restricted by the Save/Load type walk (ADR-0006 § 1.2), a restore reports through `ctx.fault` and copies into the existing block object (ADR-0006 § 2.2), division and modulus go only through `IntMath` and the repository has exactly one `integer_division` ignore (ADR-0005 § 1.4, ADR-0010 `SIM-05`), ARCH-06 forbids foreign `._member` access, and domain-3 fault codes are written "with its system ADR (ADR-0011 onward)" (ADR-0003 § 6).

Nothing about the layout can be left to the implementer. The columns are the hash input (ADR-0005), the save format (ADR-0006), the dirty-key vocabulary (ADR-0004), the read surface of eight consumer systems and the restore validator. A column added, renamed, re-typed or reordered after a build is shared is a `schema_version` bump and a migration. And the layout is the first thing the ADR-0012 phases, the ADR-0021 weld transaction and the ADR-0016 verifiers are written against.

### Constraints

- **Determinism (kernel, ADR-0005):** integer-only state; every intermediate below 2^62; dense arrays in ascending id order; no Dictionary iteration, no `sort_custom`, no `StringName` ordering; payload keys sorted; derived caches, diagnostics counters and anything non-persisted never in a payload or hash (TR-lsg-039).
- **Block contract (ADR-0003):** the block is a `RefCounted` held by its owner, never a `Resource` or `Node`; `restore` copies into the existing object because read-view facades are long-lived; every packed array in a `snapshot` payload is a duplicate; every mutator begins with `scope.open_for`; dirty keys only through `scope.mark_dirty`; faults are pre-packed integers `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local` with domain 3 fixed for the Graph.
- **Persistence (ADR-0006):** the stored payload is `var_to_bytes` of a Dictionary with `String` or `int` keys holding only `null`, `bool`, `int`, finite `float`, `String`, `Array`, `Dictionary` and `PackedByteArray`/`PackedInt32Array`/`PackedInt64Array`; `StringName`, vectors and objects are refused by the walk; failure is only `ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*)`; `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is byte-identical.
- **Source rules (ADR-0010):** `:=` banned, every `var` and `const` explicitly typed; no bare `/`, `%`, `/=`, `%=` and no untyped `min`/`max`/`clamp`/`abs`/`sign` in `src/sim/**` (`SIM-04`); exactly one `integer_division` ignore in `IntMath.trunc_div` (`SIM-05`, `PRJ-04`); no `assert` in `src/` outside `testing/` (`SIM-11`); no member, parameter or local named after a `@GlobalScope` utility or a base-class property (`SHADOWED_*` at error); accessors never return a `Packed*Array` (registry `packed_array_exposed_or_setter_tracked`); no `._member` access through a foreign receiver (`ARCH-06`); no `Node`, no signals in `src/sim/` (`SIM-01`, `SIM-13`).
- **Capacity (registry):** `MAX_GRAPH_NODES`, `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES`, `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION`, `MAX_CREW`, `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`; `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` is the kernel's and must stay at or above 128 while `graph.state` is registered. Values are cited by name here and never retyped.
- **Performance:** the Graph's hook spike share (P99 and max over one hook tick), the 0.5 ms snapshot, 2 ms restore plus `post_restore`, and the 32 KB MVP snapshot are ADR-0012's budgets (TR-lsg-025/036) measured on a release export; this ADR owns the column count behind the 32 KB.
- **Pre-existing GDD wording that this ADR must reconcile, not repeat:** LS-1 (d) asks each Graph file to open with `@warning_ignore_start("integer_division")` (contradicts `SIM-05`); LS-1/TR-lsg-002 asks for underscore-prefixed fields written only by four files (no ADR-0010 rule expresses that and ARCH-06 forbids the access); TR-lsg-024 spells `GraphFault.raise(code, subject)` with no scope argument; LS-19 says Instruments derive `load` themselves while TR-instr-027 says the Graph publishes it; TR-itemdb-033 says a restore clamps an over-cap store while LS-21 says restore never clamps.

### Requirements

- One block `graph.state`, registered last of the Item DB, Layout, Graph chain, `restore_after [layout.state]`, `schema_version` 1 (TR-lsg-001).
- Struct-of-arrays on `PackedInt64Array`/`PackedInt32Array`/`PackedByteArray` only, writer-file discipline lint-enforced (TR-lsg-002).
- A unit table with a stored width and a documented maximum for every quantity; zero floats on the path; designer floats converted once into immutable `GraphTuning` (TR-lsg-003, TR-lsg-006).
- A written classification of every member as persisted, derived, scratch or diagnostic, verified by reflection and zero-and-diff (TR-lsg-004, TR-lsg-038, TR-lsg-039).
- Conservation counters in the persisted form with an exact-equality evaluator (TR-lsg-005).
- Ids, slots and type enums that never change meaning (TR-lsg-030 residual, TR-lsg-027/028 data side, TR-lsg-029 stamps).
- A column policy for install, salvage and reinstall (TR-itemdb-016/031/040).
- A pure, allocation-free read surface with a columnar descriptor store (TR-lsg-018/019, TR-instr-027, TR-itemdb-014, TR-light-034 data side).
- The dirty-key kind table, composite packing and bucket storage (TR-lsg-020 residual).
- The domain-3 fault list, the boot-code list and the restore reason set with deterministic precedence (TR-lsg-023/024/033 residuals).
- The read-by-name discipline for registry-owned constants (TR-lsg-043).

## Decision

### 1. One block, four classes, one layer

`graph.state` is one block (the GDD's two-block alternative is rejected: a weld writes both halves, and G4 wants one snapshot, R2). It is held as four sibling `RefCounted` objects, all created once by `GraphModule.setup()` and never replaced:

| Class | File (`src/sim/graph/`) | Holds | Persisted | Hashed | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GraphState` | `graph_state.gd` | the PERSISTED columns of § 3: seven tables, `hdr`, `defs` | yes | yes | `graph_mutators.gd`, `graph_propagate.gd`, `graph_restore.gd` (the "writer files") |
| `GraphCaches` | `graph_caches.gd` | DERIVED data rebuilt from `GraphState`, Layout and the catalog: id-to-slot maps, endpoint slots, adjacency CSR, components and trees, `path_cap`, intensive values (`P`, `p_o2`, `served_pm`), the descriptor store, last-emitted buckets, `topology_version`, `topo_dirty`, lifecycle | no | no | `graph_derived.gd` only |
| `GraphScratch` | `graph_scratch.gd` | preallocated per-phase buffers: the Jacobi `next` columns and the flux and accumulator arrays ADR-0012 declares | no | no | `graph_propagate.gd` only |
| `GraphDiag` | `graph_diag.gd` | diagnostics counters: `saturations`, `stale_calls`, `gate_holds`, `stall_edges`, `footprints_dropped`, `stock_clamped`, `hash_invocations` | no | no | any Graph file (the one class every file may write) |

Splitting the non-persisted members into their own objects (instead of one wide `GraphState` with a DERIVED allowlist, the GDD's wording) makes the persisted-field check a one-line reflection test (§ 6.3): every script variable of `GraphState` is either a persisted column that `GraphSnapshot` writes into the payload or one of three holder references. TR-lsg-002 ("Graph state is a struct-of-arrays `GraphState extends RefCounted`") holds for the persisted object; the companions are the same module's.

**Other files.** `graph_module.gd` (`GraphModule`: `setup`, registration, owner callables), `graph_snapshot.gd` (builds the payload; reads `GraphState`, writes nothing), `graph_mutators.gd` (M1 to M19 and their `check_*`), `graph_propagate.gd` (ADR-0012's phases), `graph_restore.gd` (decode, validate, swap), `graph_derived.gd` (`ensure_derived`, `post_restore` derivation), `graph_faults.gd` and `graph_fault.gd`, `views/graph_view.gd`, `views/failure_filter.gd`, `views/failure_slice.gd`, `views/join_plan.gd`, `views/weld_result.gd`, `views/salvage_record.gd`, `views/instantiate_result.gd`, `ports/room_source.gd`, `testing/` (test seams). **Shared pure files** that `src/data/` loaders and the Item DB must reach without importing `src/sim/` (ADR-0007 § 1.9, ADR-0010 § 1.1): `src/shared/graph/graph_ids.gd` (`GraphIds`: every enum of § 4.7), `graph_schema.gd` (`GraphSchema`: table and column specs, payload key names, `VERSION`), `graph_limits.gd` (`GraphLimits`: code-side width limits such as `ID_MAX`, `STEP_STAMP_MAX`), `graph_rules.gd` (`connectable`, `cap_seam` and the other pure D-formulas the Item DB lints call, TR-itemdb-036), `graph_products.gd` (the D.13 product list and `product_max_assertion`). `GraphTuning` lives at `src/data/graph/graph_tuning.gd` (a frozen class built by the loader from the ADR-0007 `ScalarTable`; `src/sim/graph/` names it as an injected published type).

**Registration** (`GraphModule`, in the kernel's `BOOTING`, last of the Item DB, Layout, Graph chain; ADR-0003 § 2 and § 6, ADR-0004 § 3):

| Descriptor field | Value |
|---|---|
| `block_id` / `owner_name` | `&"graph.state"` / `&"graph"` |
| `schema_version` / `supported_versions` | 1 / `[1]` |
| `block_class` / `persist` / `persist_scope` / `scope` | `SIM` / true / `WORLD` / `SHARED` |
| `gameplay` / `interpolated` | true / false (no `commit_baseline`, no `snap_baseline`) |
| `repl_hint` | `SHARED_SUMMARY` |
| `restore_after` | `[&"layout.state"]` |
| `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state`, `post_restore`, `read_view`, `empty_view` | bound `Callable`s of `GraphModule` |
| `init_world`, `binding_source` | not registered (Web Map's `init_world` calls M1 inside its `INIT` scope; the Graph issues no binding) |
| key space | `KeySpaceDescriptor` with the nine kinds of § 10 and `quiet_writes_allowed = true` |
| fault domain | `register_fault_domain(3, &"graph", GraphFaults.NAMES)` |
| hooks | `graph.propagate.power`, `.atmo`, `.failure`, divisor 6, offsets 0, 2, 4, chained by `after:` (ADR-0012 fixes the edges and phases; the descriptors are registered here) |

The Graph registers no command (kernel H2; the domain commands live with Assembly, Interaction, Suit, Emitter State and Horror). Its published mutators are plain methods of `GraphMutators` that the composition root hands to those modules' `setup()` (ADR-0003 § 10).

### 2. The fixed-point unit system (ADR-LSG-02)

**2.1 Units.** Every stored, hashed or propagated quantity is an integer in one named unit. Scale constants come from the registry through `GraphTuning` (cited by name; never retyped here).

| Quantity | Unit and meaning | Stored as | Documented maximum (source) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gas amount (`n_o2`, `n_inert`, tank `stock` for O2) | mGU: milli gas units, scale `GAS_SCALE`; 1 GU gives 0.1 kPa in one tile | `PackedInt64Array` | per compartment `n_max(c) = P_MAX x V_c x GAS_SCALE` (D.13); tank: the def's `stock_cap`, hard ceiling `GraphTuning.max_stock_gas` |
| Pressure, partial pressure | dkPa; **derived only** (`P = f(n, V)`, D.3) | never stored | `P_MAX`; standard `STD_PRESSURE_DKPA` |
| Volume | tiles, from Layout (`V`); **derived copy** | `GraphCaches` | `V_max` in `GraphTuning` (D.13) |
| Temperature | mC; compartment `T`, coolant `t_cool` | `PackedInt32Array` | `abs(dT)` maximum in D.13; ambient `T_AMB_MC` |
| Thermal remainder | `t_rem`, `tc_rem`: dJ carried so that `U = T x C + t_rem` is exact (two signed steps truncate toward zero, all others floor) | `PackedInt32Array` | below the compartment's `C` (bounded by `V_max x C_TILE`) |
| Power, energy | W is dJ per step; battery `stock` in dJ; `radiated_dj`, `produced_dj` | W in `PackedInt32Array`; stocks and counters in `PackedInt64Array` | per-field maxima in `GraphTuning` (D.13) |
| Liquids | mL (coolant, fuel); fuel burn counter in micro-mL (10^6 uml = 1 mL) | `PackedInt64Array` | the def's `stock_cap`; hard ceiling `GraphTuning.max_stock_liquid` |
| Integrity | bp, 0 to `HP_FULL` | `PackedInt32Array` | `HP_FULL` |
| Fractions | permille (served, run, throttle, circulation, intensity) | `PackedInt32Array` | 1000, plus overload up to the D.13 bound |
| Opening area | milli flow units on the gas path (`A_m = 1000 x flow units`, D.1); `area` and `area_max` are stored in flow units (64 = one standard door) | `PackedInt32Array` | `A_HOLE_MAX`, D.13 `A_m` bound |
| Time | **Graph steps**: `step_no = floor_div(T, GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)`; every persisted stamp (`fail_since_step`, `built_step`, `patched_at_step`, ...) is in steps, never kernel ticks | `PackedInt32Array` (stamps), `int` (header) | `STEP_STAMP_MAX` (`GraphLimits`, 2^30) |
| Enums, flags, bands | small closed sets | `PackedByteArray` | the `GraphIds` domain of each |
| Ids, slots, indices | non-negative ints | `PackedInt32Array` | `ID_MAX` (`GraphLimits`, 2^24); caps `MAX_GRAPH_NODES`, `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` |
| Conservation counters, `next_*`, `last_step_*` | exact integer tallies | `PackedInt64Array` (per section), `int` (header) | no stored cap; D.13 bounds their growth rate |

**2.2 Width rule (why three array types).** `PackedInt64Array` holds every conserved or extensive quantity and every counter, because the GDD's gas maximum alone exceeds what a later content change could be allowed to wrap, and because all arithmetic is 64-bit anyway. `PackedInt32Array` holds ids, indices, step stamps, basis points, permille and the short physical quantities listed above, each with a declared maximum far below 2^31. `PackedByteArray` holds enums and flag bytes. A 32-bit store truncates silently (probe (g), ADR-0005 P9, P17), so the rule is: **arithmetic is done in plain `int`, and a value is range-checked against its column maximum before it is stored into an `int32` or `uint8` column**; the check is the mutator or phase's responsibility, is bounded by the column spec of § 3, and a violation is the numeric soft invariant of § 8.3. Values copied from the catalog into 32-bit columns (port caps, `req_max`, `hp_start`) are checked once at boot against the column maxima (`GRAPH_BOOT_COLUMN_RANGE`, § 8.4).

**2.3 Arithmetic discipline** (ADR-0005 § 1.3 to § 1.5, ADR-0010 `SIM-03`/`SIM-04`/`SIM-05`):
- Every flux is a non-negative magnitude with an explicit direction (LS-1 (d)), so every division on the propagation path has a non-negative numerator and `IntMath.floor_div` equals truncation. The two signed thermal remainder steps call `IntMath.trunc_div` by name.
- There is **no file-level `@warning_ignore_start("integer_division")` in `src/sim/graph/`**. LS-1 (d) asked for one and S0-b was to verify it; ADR-0005 P6 shows it compiles, but ADR-0010 `SIM-05`/`PRJ-04` allow exactly one `integer_division` ignore in `src/`, and `SIM-04` bans the `/` and `%` tokens outright, so the annotation would have nothing to silence and would itself be a finding. The cost is the one ADR-0005 measured (`floor_div` is about 12 times a bare operator, P14); whether that matters in the phases is S1's answer, and the remedy it names (inlining a proven non-negative form in named hot files) is an ADR-0010 amendment decided on that measurement (§ Open Questions 1). This is a `gdd_sync` item (LS-1 (d), TR-lsg-003 wording).
- `min`, `max`, `clamp`, `abs` and `sign` are written with the typed builtins `mini`, `maxi`, `clampi`, `absi`, `signi` (probe (a)). ADR-0010 `SIM-04` bans the untyped names and is silent about the typed ones; the Graph cannot be written without them, so this ADR relies on them and asks ADR-0010 to say so (foundation ask 2).
- Laws are linear or piecewise-linear integer tables; no `sqrt`, `exp`, `pow`, `sin`; per-step decay is `x -= floor_div(x * k_ppm, 1000000)` (LS-1 (g)). No float, no `Vector2`, no `Vector2i` (32-bit components, ADR-0005 P17) in any Graph signature or column.
- **Overflow is designed out, not detected.** `src/shared/graph/graph_products.gd` holds the D.13 product list as code (`PRODUCTS`: ordered operand-name pairs, running three-factor products asserted pairwise) and `product_max_assertion(tuning) -> int` (0 on success, else the index of the first pair with `max_a x max_b >= 2^62`). The maxima are `GraphTuning.max_*` constants; the loader calls the function in stage 1 and a violation is `GRAPH_BOOT_PRODUCT_OVERFLOW(a, b)` (domain 2). The worst product is `G_OPEN x A_m x abs(g)` with thin margin (D.13); raising `GAS_SCALE` or `V_max` trips boot rather than wrapping in play.
- `GraphView.step_no()` is `IntMath.floor_div(clock.tick(), tuning.graph_step_ticks)`, a pure function of `T` available at any call site (Failure & Trail compares it with its poll cache, FT-15; the Item DB's `validate_instance` compares against it, TR-itemdb-014). `hdr.last_step_no` is the last step whose power hook completed and is persisted for restore; the two differ only between a tick and its first hook.

### 3. Tables and columns (ADR-LSG-01)

**3.1 The table set.** Seven tables, a def-name pair and a scalar header. Rows of nodes, ports, edges, compartments, seams and sections are **dense, append-only and ordered by ascending id**; a table's arrays all have exactly the table's row count (`size()` equals the row count; there is no spare capacity in persisted columns, so `duplicate()` of a column is the exact payload and a length mismatch is detectable). Structural mutators grow tables with `resize` (the only allocation outside the steady state).

| Table | Row = | Row order | Row count source | Bytes per row (columns of § 3.2 to § 3.8) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nodes` | one node slot, tombstones kept | ascending `id` | `next_node_id` allocations | 85 |
| `ports` | one port of one node, contiguous per node | ascending `(node slot, local order)` | allocated with the node | 10 |
| `edges` | one edge slot, tombstones kept | ascending `id` | `next_edge_id` allocations | 73 |
| `comps` | one COMPARTMENT node (EXTERIOR has no row) | ascending `node_id` | one per COMPARTMENT node | 56 |
| `seams` | one SeamRecord, `CUT` records kept | ascending `id` | `next_seam_id` allocations | 63 (+ list entries) |
| `sections` | one section record | ascending `id` | section creations | 150 |
| `queues` | four parallel groups: `pending_draw`, `pending_load`, `pending_trace`, `draw_grant` | arrival order | bounded (§ 3.8) | 8 to 16 per entry |
| `defs` | the interned def-name CSR pair `off` (`int32`), `utf8` (`uint8`) | append-only | one entry per distinct `def_id` ever installed | n/a |
| `hdr` | named scalars (a Dictionary of `int` values, not a packed array) | n/a | n/a | n/a |

**Why a fixed `ports` CSR and not `MAX_PORTS_PER_NODE`.** A node's ports are the contiguous run `[port_first, port_first + port_count)` of the `ports` table. Port counts differ widely (a junction has many, a lamp one), so a fixed per-node maximum either wastes most of a large table or caps content; the run costs two columns on `nodes` and keeps the table dense. Ports are allocated with their node (from the section template's hardpoint), never inserted later, so the run never moves. **Why `comps` is a separate table keyed to a node:** a COMPARTMENT is a node (kind 1) so an OPENING edge can name it as an endpoint like any other node; its atmosphere columns live in `comps` (one row per COMPARTMENT node) so the node table does not carry five dead columns for 90 percent of its rows. **The compartment id `cid` is the compartment's node id** (one id space; § 4.4). EXTERIOR (kind 2, node id 0, section 0) has no `comps` row: its pressure and temperature are the constants `P_EXT` and `T_AMB_MC`.

**3.2 `nodes` columns** (`int32` unless noted):

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | i32 | node id, never reused |
| `kind` | u8 | `GraphIds.NODE_KIND` (LS-3) |
| `flags` | u8 | bit 0 TOMBSTONE, 1 HAS_WARN, 2 EXOGENOUS (last damage cause), 3 BREAKER_CLOSED (CABLE_JUNCTION), 4 FATIGUED (hull), 5 EXPOSED (hull), 6 STUB (hull stub of a RAGGED cut), 7 reserved (zero) |
| `section_id` | i32 | owning section; 0 only for EXTERIOR |
| `def_ix` | i32 | index into `defs` (0 = none: COMPARTMENT, EXTERIOR, HULL_SEGMENT, ABSENT, SALVAGED) |
| `state` | u8 | `GraphIds.NODE_STATE` 0 OK .. 5 ABSENT (LS-10) |
| `hp`, `hp_cap` | i32 | bp, 0 to `HP_FULL`; `hp_cap` defaults to `HP_FULL` |
| `forced_mode`, `forced_next` | u8 | forced mode and the cascade queue (LS-12), mode ids |
| `fail_since`, `warn_since`, `mode_since`, `isolated_at`, `thaw_until`, `patched_at` | i32 | the six step stamps of LS-3 (back-dated values may be at or below 0, so these are signed); `warn_since` is meaningful only while HAS_WARN |
| `mode_key` | u8 | `(mode << 3) \| sev` of the dominant descriptor, 0 = none (`GRAPH_BOOT_MODE_ID` keeps the largest mode id at or below 31) |
| `compartment_id` | i32 | cid of the room the node sits in (a COMPARTMENT's own id) |
| `port_first`, `port_count` | i32, u8 | the node's port run in `ports` |
| `stock` | **i64** | store content in the store's own unit: BATTERY dJ, O2_TANK mGU, RESERVOIR and FUEL_TANK mL; 0 for every other kind |
| `req`, `req_max` | i32 | the owner-set request and its copy-at-install ceiling: LOAD and SCRUBBER `req_w`/`req_max`, PUMP `throttle_pm`, VENT `setpoint_pp`, REACTOR `out_w` |
| `aux_a`, `aux_b` | i32 | kind payload: REACTOR `fuel_rem`, `starve_steps`; LOAD `energised_at_step`, 0; RESERVOIR `t_cool`, `tc_rem`; HULL_SEGMENT `bound_compartment`, `tiles`; all others 0 |
| `tier`, `subtype` | u8 | LOAD priority tier and subtype (HEATER, LAMP, DOOR_MOTOR, ...); 0 elsewhere |

**The overlay is normative**: each kind-specific reading of `stock`, `req`, `req_max`, `aux_a`, `aux_b`, `tier`, `subtype` is exposed only through a named accessor on `GraphView` or a writer (`reactor_fuel_rem(slot)`, `reservoir_t_cool(slot)`, `hull_bound_compartment(slot)`), never by raw column index outside the writer and snapshot files. The alternative (a side table per kind) costs an extra row-index map per table for the sake of a few bytes per row on about 105 nodes (Alternative 6).

**3.3 `ports` columns:** `type` (i32, `GraphIds.PORT_TYPE`, LS-4), `cap` (i32, loop units per step, copied at install; **retained when a module is salvaged or a seam is cut** so a SEVERED stub leaks at `OPEN_END_RATE_PM` of the port's cap), `local` (u8, `local_index`), `flags` (u8: bit 0 OPEN_END, bit 1 CAPPED).

**3.4 `edges` columns** (`int32` unless noted): `id`; `kind` (u8, LS-5); `loop` (u8); `flags` (u8: bit 0 TOMBSTONE, 1 HAS_WARN, 2 EXOGENOUS, 3 OPEN (VALVE), 4 CAPPED, 5 EXPOSED (DUCT), 6 STRAIN_GAS, 7 STRAIN_HEAT (the two SEAL_STRAIN hysteresis bits of a stored OPENING, D.14)); `a_node`, `b_node` (node ids), `a_port`, `b_port` (u8 local indices); `section_id`; `hp`, `hp_cap`; `state`, `forced_mode`, `forced_next`, `mode_key` (u8); `fail_since`, `warn_since`, `mode_since`, `isolated_at`, `thaw_until`, `patched_at`; `seam_id` (0 = none); `cap` (loop units per step); `e0` (DUCT `len`, OPENING `area`), `e1` (OPENING `area_max`). OPENING `door_state` is derived from `area` (LS-19) and never stored. **Edge endpoints are persisted as ids**, not slots; the endpoint slots are DERIVED (§ 4.2).

**3.5 `comps` columns:** `node_id` (i32, the cid), `room_ref` (i32, `layout_room_ref`, Layout's room id), `n_o2`, `n_inert` (**i64**), `t` (i32 mC), `t_rem` (i32), `fuel_puddle` (i32 mL), `band_o2`, `band_p`, `band_t` (u8, hysteresis memory), `p_prev` (i32, the previous run's `P`), `warn_o2`, `warn_p`, `warn_t` (i32 step stamps), `warn_bits` (u8). Derived and never here: `V`, `exposed_tiles` (Layout), `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, `pressure_trend`.

**3.6 `seams` columns:** `id`, `section_a`, `section_b`, `q`, `hp` (the seam's weld quality x 10), `leak_bp`, `l_seam`, `built_step`, `mode_since` (i32); `mode_key`, `state` (ACTIVE, CUT), `boundary` (SEALED, RAGGED; 0 while ACTIVE) (u8); and three CSR pairs into flat lists `edge_ids`, `opening_ids`, `stub_ids` (`edge_first`/`edge_count`, `open_first`/`open_count`, `stub_first`/`stub_count`, all i32). A SeamRecord is never deleted: a cut turns it into a tombstone with state CUT, its lists intact (the cut-hole ids `seam_view` reports). **The hull stubs of a RAGGED cut are ordinary HULL_SEGMENT node rows appended at the cut** (flags STUB, `hp` 2500 as LS-16, `aux_a` the bound compartment), listed in `stub_ids`; the GDD's "hull-stub records ... no new persisted field" is therefore satisfied by existing columns, and `cut_detach` can append rows, so ADR-0012/0021's `can_detach` must include `CAPACITY` (cross-ADR assumption).

**3.7 `sections` columns:** `id`, `dormant_since`, `rate_pm`, `stress_pm`, `stress_until` (i32); `kind` (u8: HOME, DERELICT); `flags` (u8: bit 0 DORMANT); and sixteen `int64` counters: `vented_mgu`, `radiated_dj`, `spilled_cool_ml`, `produced_mgu`, `breathed_mgu`, `produced_dj`, `burned_uml`, `spilled_heat_mdj`, and `disc_` and `wd_` for each of the four media (gas mGU, coolant mL, fuel mL, energy dJ): `disc_mgu`, `disc_cool_ml`, `disc_fuel_ml`, `disc_dj`, `wd_mgu`, `wd_cool_ml`, `wd_fuel_ml`, `wd_dj`. (LS-21 names `discarded_*` and `withdrawn_*` "per medium" and M16 is legal on a BATTERY in dJ; the energy medium is the fourth. Open Question 4 asks the GDD to confirm.)

**3.8 `queues`, `defs`, `hdr`.**
- `pending_draw`: `draw_comp` (i32 cid), `draw_crew` (i32), `draw_mgu` (**i64**), arrival order, at most `MAX_CREW` x compartment-count entries.
- `pending_load`: `load_node` (i32), `load_req` (i32), arrival order, at most `GraphTuning.load_queue_max` (TR-lsg-017: 64; a registry gap, § Open Questions 5).
- `pending_trace`: `trace_kind` (u8), `trace_subject` (i32), `trace_mag` (i32), arrival order, at most `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` per run across callers.
- `draw_grant`: `grant_crew` (i32), `grant_req`, `grant_got` (**i64**), the last applied grants, one per crew member.
- `defs`: `off` has `def_count + 1` entries with `off[0] = 0` and `off[1] = 0` (entry 0 is the empty string, so `def_ix` 0 means none); entry `k` is `utf8[off[k] : off[k+1]]`. Append-only; an entry stays after its module is salvaged.
- `hdr`: `next_node_id`, `next_edge_id`, `next_seam_id`, `next_section_id`, `last_step_no`, `last_step_power`, `last_step_atmo`, `last_step_failure`. **Individual named `int` values in a Dictionary**, not a packed array of slots: eight values do not justify a slot-order document, a restore diff names the key, and ADR-0005 § 3.6's "more than about 250 scalar fields" threshold is about arrays of rows, not a header.

**3.9 Canonical zeros.** A row has exactly one encoding per logical state: **every column that does not apply to a row's kind or state holds the canonical zero** (0, or `HP_FULL` for `hp_cap` of a live subject only where LS-3 defines it). A mutator that changes a row's kind-dependent role (install, salvage, discard, cut) zeroes the columns the new role does not use; a tombstoned row keeps `id`, `kind` and `section_id` and zeroes everything else; `GraphSchema` records the "zero when" predicate per column and the restore validator and a debug check enforce it (a non-zero in an inapplicable column is `GRAPH_RESTORE_INVARIANT(canonical_zero)`).

**3.10 Payload shape.** `snapshot(ctx)` calls `ctx.put(payload)` where `payload` is **one Dictionary with `String` keys**: `"hdr"` (a Dictionary of the eight `int` values) and one nested Dictionary per table (`"nodes"`, `"ports"`, `"edges"`, `"comps"`, `"seams"`, `"sections"`, `"queues"`, `"defs"`) mapping column name to a **duplicate** of the packed column (ADR-0003 snapshot contract). Nested, not flat `"nodes.hp"` keys: the key text is shorter, the restore validator iterates tables by name, and ADR-0005's sorted key order applies at each level, so the hash order is `comps, defs, edges, hdr, nodes, ports, queues, sections, seams` and within a table the column names ascending. **Payload keys are `String`, never `StringName`**: the Save/Load walk rejects `StringName` as a key or value, and a `StringName` key round-trips as a `StringName` through `var_to_bytes` (probe (h)); the `GraphSchema` name constants are `String` constants. Renaming, adding, removing or re-typing a table, column or header key is a `schema_version` bump and a migration function (§ 7.5). `GraphSchema.fingerprint()` returns H64 over the sorted `table.column:type` lines; the committed value in `tests/fixtures/graph/schema.fingerprint` may change only together with a `schema_version` bump (CI), mirroring ADR-0006 § 2.6.

**3.11 Size.** The probed fixture of Engine Compatibility (i) gives **29.7 KB canonical bytes for 105 nodes, 150 edges, 270 ports and 14 compartments** (the loaded set home plus both derelicts, about 250 subjects as LS-26 and S3 count them), against the 32 KB ceiling of TR-lsg-036 (ADR-0012's budget): about 7 percent headroom, and 32 KB is reached near 114 nodes and 163 edges. The MVP roster fits; a fourth derelict loaded at once does not. If the fixture is measured above the ceiling, the levers in order are: (1) move `thaw_until`, `isolated_at` and `warn_since`/`mode_since` of non-fluid subjects into a fluid-subject side table (about 1.8 KB at this roster, the largest block of dead zeros); (2) merge the two `int32` step stamps that are always read together; (3) ask the owner to raise the ceiling with this measurement. None is taken now; the column count is a reviewed schema, not a place to guess.

# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## Architecture Decision Records (`docs/architecture/`)

Use the ADR template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`

**Required sections:** Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences,
ADR Dependencies, Engine Compatibility, GDD Requirements Addressed

**Status lifecycle:** `Proposed` → `Accepted` → `Superseded`
- Never skip `Accepted` — stories referencing a `Proposed` ADR are auto-blocked
- Use `/architecture-decision` to create ADRs through the guided flow

**TR Registry:** `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
- Stable requirement IDs (e.g. `TR-movement-001`) that link GDD requirements to stories
- Never renumber existing IDs — only append new ones
- Updated by `/architecture-review` Phase 8

**Control Manifest:** `docs/architecture/control-manifest.md`
- Flat programmer rules sheet: Required / Forbidden / Guardrails per layer
- Date-stamped `Manifest Version:` in header
- Stories embed this version; `/story-done` checks for staleness

**Validation:** Run `/architecture-review` after completing a set of ADRs.

## Engine Reference (`docs/engine-reference/`)

Version-pinned engine API snapshots. **Always check here before using any
engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

### 4. Append-only topology identity (ADR-LSG-04)

**4.1 The rules.**
1. **Ids come only from the four persisted counters** (`next_node_id`, `next_edge_id`, `next_seam_id`, `next_section_id`), which only increase. A counter is never decremented, not by an error path, not by a fault, not by a restore (a restore sets it from the payload, which the validator checks is above every id in the table, `GRAPH_RESTORE_COUNTER`). An id is never reused after its row is tombstoned or its section discarded.
2. **Slot order is id order.** A new row is appended at the end of its table with an id above every existing id; nothing is inserted or moved; nothing renumbers. There is **no compaction in the MVP**: removal is a tombstone flag (§ 3.9), and capacity (`MAX_GRAPH_NODES`, `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES`) counts slots including tombstones, which is what `CAPACITY` in `can_join` and M1 tests. VS-A's order-preserving compaction (LS-17) is out of scope; § Risks 6 records what it would break.
3. **A weld only appends** edge rows, one SeamRecord row, its list entries and its OPENING edges; it never touches an existing row's id, slot or endpoint (TR-lsg-027, data side). `cut_detach` tombstones edge rows and flips the SeamRecord to CUT; a RAGGED cut also appends stub HULL_SEGMENT rows (§ 3.6). `discard_section` tombstones every row of the section; mass leaves through the `disc_*` counters (TR-lsg-028, data side).
4. **Ids are bounded by construction:** every allocation tests `next_id < GraphLimits.ID_MAX` (2^24) and the table caps; an infallible mutator that would exceed either raises `GraphFaults.ID_SPACE_EXHAUSTED` (a defect, since the `check_*` that precedes it tests `CAPACITY`). 2^24 keeps `L/<loop>/<anchor>` and `F/<subject_ref>` keys inside the 32-bit key id (§ 10) and keeps `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` far below the 2^20 the RNG subject field allows.
5. **A stale id is harmless.** An id that is at or above its counter, or was never allocated, or names a tombstone, resolves to slot -1: a Class B mutator no-ops and returns 0/false, a Class A `check_*` returns its `UNKNOWN`/`NOT_*` reason, and a read returns the neutral value. Nothing indexes an array with an unchecked id.

**4.2 Id-to-slot is derived.** Persisted references between rows are ids (edge endpoints, `compartment_id`, `section_id`, `bound_compartment`, queue subjects). `GraphCaches` holds the dense maps `slot_of_node[id]`, `slot_of_edge[id]`, `slot_of_seam[id]`, `slot_of_section[id]` (`PackedInt32Array` indexed by id, -1 when absent, sized to `next_id`), the endpoint slot columns `edge_a_slot`, `edge_b_slot`, and the lookup-only `Dictionary[int, int]` `comp_of_room_ref` (never iterated). All are rebuilt eagerly by `ensure_derived()` after every structural mutator and in `post_restore` (§ 6), so a read never rebuilds in an arbitrary presentation frame. While no compaction exists, id equals slot for nodes and edges allocated contiguously, but **no code may assume it**: every access goes through the map, so VS-A compaction changes the cache and the allocator, not the callers.

**4.3 Cross-block references to Graph ids.** Layout stores `graph_ref_base {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` per section; Interaction and the Perception Filter hold node and edge ids; Suit holds a compartment id through `actor_section`. All are plain ids resolved through `slot_of_*`; a Graph id never leaves the block as an array position (ADR-0005 § 3.6).

**4.4 Compartment identity.** `cid` is the **node id of the COMPARTMENT node**. M1 allocates a section's node ids contiguously in template order with the section's COMPARTMENT nodes first, in Layout room order, so `comp_base == node_base` and `cid(room k) == comp_base + k`; the returned `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` keep the shape LS-18 and Layout's `graph_ref_base` expect. `layout_room_ref` is Layout's block-local room id, stored in `comps.room_ref`; Layout owns `section_id` and `room_id` allocation and M1 takes `section_id` as an argument and only advances `next_section_id` to `max(section_id) + 1` (cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0013). `section_id` 0 is reserved for the world-level EXTERIOR; real sections start at 1.

**4.5 Ports.** A port is identified by `(node id, local_index)`; its row is in the node's run and the run never moves. SALVAGED and ABSENT nodes keep their ports (type, cap, local index) so an M5 reinstall can match the hardpoint.

**4.6 `default_state`.** The EMPTY block has the EXTERIOR node row (id 0, kind 2, section 0, state OK, no ports), the four counters at 1, `last_step_*` at 0, and every other table empty (LS: "no sections, counters at 1"). A registered-but-unrestored block therefore hashes the same on every run.

**4.7 Stable type ids.** `src/shared/graph/graph_ids.gd` (`GraphIds`) holds every enum that reaches a payload, as `const` integers: `LOOP` (0..5), `NODE_KIND`, `PORT_TYPE`, `EDGE_KIND`, `MODE` (1..10 and 20..27), `NODE_STATE` (0..5), `BAND_O2`, `BAND_P`, `BAND_T`, `SEAM_STATE`, `SEAM_BOUNDARY`, `SECTION_KIND`, `LOAD_TIER`, `LOAD_SUBTYPE`, `TRACE_KIND`, `SUBJECT_KIND`, `CAUSE`, `MEDIUM`, `ACOUSTIC`. ADR-0007 § 3.2 already makes these the baseline that `assets/data/graph/` must equal (`GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID`, domain 2) and gives them no ledger, assigning their stability to this ADR. The stability mechanism: **a committed `assets/data/graph/ids.lock.json`** in the ADR-0007 ledger format (`space`, `format`, `state`, `pairs`, `retired_ids`), one `space` per enum above, generated from `GraphIds`, checked with the existing `LedgerCheck.verify` at boot and by the `LEDGER_NOT_APPEND_ONLY` base-revision gate in CI (WARN while `PRE_RELEASE`, ERROR once `SHIPPED`, flipped by the same one-way commit as the other ledgers). A new value is a new number; a retired value goes in `retired_ids`; an existing pair never changes. This adds one lock file and no new mechanism to ADR-0007 (foundation ask 4). The persisted enums (`band_*`, `state`, `boundary`, ...) are in the lock because they are written into saves, not because content authors extend them.

### 5. Node-slot lifecycle: what carries, what resets, what is read live

Item DB IDB-18 and Interaction/Assembly use M5 `install_module`, M6 `salvage_node` and M7 `repair_step`; the Item DB calls no mutator. The columns of § 3.2 behave as follows (TR-itemdb-016, 031, 040; ADR-0021 orders the calls, this table is the data contract):

| Column group | M1 `instantiate_section` | M5 `install_module` (ABSENT or SALVAGED to OK) | M6 `salvage_node` (to SALVAGED) |
|---|---|---|---|
| identity (`id`, `kind`, `section_id`, `compartment_id`, ports run) | set from template | untouched | untouched |
| `def_ix` | interned from the template (0 for a bare authored VENT/LOAD, which M6 refuses with `NOT_SALVAGEABLE`) | interned from the installed `def_id` | cleared to 0 (the `SalvageRecord` carries the `def_id` string) |
| `hp`, `hp_cap`, `patched_at` | template (`hp_start`; `hp_cap` `HP_FULL`; `patched_at` 0) | **from the arguments**: `hp_start`, `hp_cap`, `patched_at_step` (a patched module returns capped and keeps its absolute decay clock; only a spent repair part, M7 FULL, lifts a cap) | recorded in the `SalvageRecord`, then zeroed |
| `stock` | template (a store installs empty unless authored) | **0** | the remaining stock moves into the section's `disc_*` counter (conservation closes), then **0** |
| `req`, `req_max` | template defaults | **copy-at-install**: `req` and `req_max` from the def (`req_w`, `req_max`), setpoints (`throttle_pm`, `setpoint_pp`) take the Graph's fresh defaults, never the salvaged module's | zeroed |
| port `cap` | template | **copy-at-install** from the def's ports | retained (SEVERED stub rate) |
| port `flags` | template | OPEN_END and CAPPED cleared | OPEN_END set on fluid ports (the connected edges' ends are SEVERED) |
| `state`, `forced_mode`, `forced_next`, `mode_key`, `fail_since`, `warn_since`, `mode_since`, `isolated_at`, `thaw_until`, HAS_WARN | template | **re-derived from `hp` by the next phase 9**: `state` FAILED when `hp` is at or below `HP_FAIL`; a reinstall never raises `hp` and never clears an hp-caused failure; stamps and flags zeroed | zeroed |
| `state` itself | per template | OK on install, then phase 9 re-derives | SALVAGED |
| kind payload (`aux_a`, `aux_b`, `tier`, `subtype`) | template | from the def where a def field applies (LOAD tier and subtype), else 0 | zeroed |

**Read-live fields** (`waste_permille`, `out_w_rated`, `stock_cap`, `repair_part_id`, the emits record) are **never copied into a persisted column**; they are read through `def_ix` to the immutable `ItemDef` at each use. A hot loop may read them through a DERIVED per-slot column (`caches.def_waste_pm[slot]`, `caches.def_out_w_rated[slot]`) rebuilt by `ensure_derived`, which is a cache of the frozen catalog and not a copy of state. Because the catalog is frozen for the process lifetime, a catalogue tuning edit takes effect at the next start through exactly that rebuild, so a save restores unchanged (TR-itemdb-032).

### 6. Persisted, derived, scratch, diagnostic

**6.1 Store extensive, derive intensive** (LS-1 (c), TR-lsg-004). Persisted: the extensive quantities and the hysteresis memory. Derived: everything a pure function of persisted state, the catalog and Layout.

| Class | Members |
|---|---|
| **PERSISTED** (`GraphState`) | `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `t`, `t_rem`, `fuel_puddle`; `stock`, `tc_rem`, `t_cool`, `fuel_rem`, `out_w`; `hp`, `hp_cap`, `state`, `forced_mode`, `forced_next`; the six step stamps and `mode_key`; `thaw_until`; the band memory `band_o2/p/t`, `p_prev`, the warn trackers `warn_o2/p/t`, `warn_bits`; the two STRAIN bits per stored OPENING; `req`, `breaker`, `open`, `area`, `capped`, `open_end`; the section counters; the four `pending_*`/`draw_grant` queues; the id counters, `last_step_*`, the def table |
| **DERIVED** (`GraphCaches`) | `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, `pressure_trend`; `V`, `exposed_tiles`; `served_pm`, `circ`, `run_pm`; components, trees, `path_cap`, degrees, adjacency CSR, `power_use` window; the failure-descriptor store; last-emitted dirty buckets; id-to-slot maps and endpoint slots; the def-row and `def_waste_pm` columns; `topology_version`, `topo_dirty`, lifecycle (`EMPTY`/`LIVE`) |
| **SCRATCH** (`GraphScratch`) | per-phase buffers sized by structural mutators: the Jacobi `next` columns (§ 6.2) and the accumulators and flux arrays ADR-0012 declares |
| **DIAGNOSTIC** (`GraphDiag`) | `saturations` (indexed by a `SatField` enum), `stale_calls`, `gate_holds`, `stall_edges`, `footprints_dropped`, `stock_clamped`, `hash_invocations` |

`P`, `p_o2` and `served_pm` are recomputed at the end of their phase and in `post_restore`, and a read returns the cached value, so `read_view` stays pure (TR-lsg-018) and the first presented frame after a restore is correct (LS: `post_restore` derives `served_pm` and the descriptor list from restored state).

**6.2 Aliasing and the Jacobi pair.** S0-a, the packed-array aliasing question the GDD left open, is **closed for the data model by ADR-0005 P7 and probes (c), (d)**: a `Packed*Array` is shared by reference by assignment, by argument and by a getter, an element write through any alias is visible through all, and only `duplicate()` isolates (by deferred copy-on-write, probe (e)). Consequences, as rules: **(1)** a function may take a local alias of a column for reads and writes within one phase (no one resizes during a phase); **(2)** an alias is never kept across a kernel call, a `snapshot`, a `restore` or a structural mutator (`resize` and member re-assignment would orphan it); **(3)** a snapshot is never a local alias: it is a `duplicate()` placed in the payload (ADR-0003); **(4)** Jacobi's "start-of-phase snapshot" is two member arrays, `GraphState` column (`cur`) and a `GraphScratch` `next` array of the same length, swapped by reference at the phase end (`var t: PackedInt64Array = state_col; state_col = scratch_next; scratch_next = t`, allocation-free, probe (c)). Which columns are double-buffered and when the swap happens is ADR-0012's; the data model's contribution is that `next` arrays live in `GraphScratch`, are sized with the table, and that anything holding a column reference reads it through the member each time (the `GraphView` facade reads `state` members, never a cached array), so a swap cannot strand a reader.

**6.3 The persisted-field check (TR-lsg-038).** Two CI checks, both in `tests/unit/graph/`:
- **Method A, reflection.** Enumerate `GraphState.new().get_property_list()` filtered by `PROPERTY_USAGE_SCRIPT_VARIABLE` (probed: includes underscore members, in declaration order). Every name must be either a column that `GraphSnapshot.build()` writes into the payload (the check builds a payload from a populated state and compares the key sets against `GraphSchema`) or one of the three holder references `_caches`, `_scratch`, `_diag`. The same enumeration over `GraphCaches` and `GraphScratch` compares against the checked-in allowlist `tests/fixtures/graph/derived_members.json` (one line per member, reason and rebuilding function), which fails on any member not listed and on any listed member that does not exist.
- **Method B, zero and diff.** For each `GraphCaches` member, zero (or `reset()` the cache) in a copy of a mid-fault state, run one step, and assert the copy's `state_hash` equals the unmodified control's after `ensure_derived()` is allowed to run; a step that reads a cache it did not first recompute shows as a differing hash. `GraphScratch` members are cleared the same way. Both must pass.

**6.4 Conservation (TR-lsg-005).** The sixteen section counters of § 3.7 are the persisted half of LS-1 (e). `src/shared/graph/graph_invariants.gd` holds pure evaluators over a `GraphState` read only: `gas_total(state, section_id)`, `heat_total_mdj(state, section_id)`, `coolant_total(state, section_id)`, `fuel_total_uml(state, section_id)`, each the left side of the LS-1 (e) equality for that medium (gas: `n_o2 + n_inert` over compartments, plus O2_TANK stock, plus `vented_mgu`, `breathed_mgu`, `disc_mgu` and `wd_mgu`, minus `produced_mgu`; heat in milli-dJ over compartments' `T x C + t_rem` and every RESERVOIR's heat store, plus `1000 x (radiated_dj - produced_dj)` and `spilled_heat_mdj`; coolant and fuel as LS-1 (e) gives, fuel in micro-mL with `fuel_rem` subtracted). **A test asserts each total equals its value at the section's instantiation after every step of every fixture, on a running ship with sources, sinks and crew active.** The baseline is held by the test (it is a function of the template), not persisted, which keeps the LS-21 field list unchanged. The exact term lists stay in the GDD; the evaluators are the executable form and are the thing a reviewer diffs against LS-1 (e).

**6.5 Perception independence (TR-lsg-018).** `src/sim/graph/**` imports nothing from `src/presentation/` (`ARCH-02`), names none of `PERCEPTION_OUT`, `perceived(`, `PerceptionRef` (ADR-0010 `READ-03` token list for the directory), and requests no `PERCEPTION_OUT` view; a mutator argument is an id, a magnitude, an enum or a plan (LS-22). The fixture of LS-22 (a degraded ship with and without a Perception block set to "all OK") asserts `state_hash` of `graph.state` is identical.

### 7. Snapshot, restore and `post_restore`

**7.1 Snapshot.** `GraphSnapshot.build(state, out)` walks `GraphSchema` and, for each table and column, places `column.duplicate()` into the nested Dictionary, then `ctx.put(payload)`. It reads nothing but `GraphState`, includes no derived or diagnostic member, and the same function feeds `canonical_encode` (the kernel encodes; the Graph has no byte writer, ADR-0005 § 3.1). A snapshot may be taken on any tick, which is why the queues, `draw_grant`, hook cursors and hysteresis memory are persisted.

**7.2 Restore** (`GraphRestore.restore(data, stored_version, ctx)`, two-phase, ADR-0006 § 2.2). Phase 1 decodes `data` into a fresh scratch `GraphState` (every column `duplicate()`d out of `data`, no reference kept into it) and validates it. Phase 2, on success only, assigns the scratch columns into the live `GraphState` member by member (the object is never replaced, so facades stay valid), calls `GraphCaches.reset()` and marks the block `RESTORING` done. Any failure is `ctx.fault(GraphFaults.RESTORE_<name>, detail)` with the live state untouched; there is no clamp and no partial apply. **Validation runs in a fixed order and the first failure wins**, so a given corrupt input always yields the same reason (the 1,000-mutation fuzz of the GDD depends on it):

| Step | Check | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `stored_version` is 1 | `RESTORE_BAD_VERSION(stored, supported)` |
| 2 | exact table and column key sets (and `hdr` keys), `String` keys, expected element types | `RESTORE_BAD_TAG(key)` |
| 3 | all columns of a table have the same length; CSR runs (`ports`, seam lists, `defs`) lie inside their arrays | `RESTORE_BAD_LENGTH(field, expected, got)` |
| 4 | enum columns lie in their `GraphIds` domain | `RESTORE_BAD_ENUM(field, slot, value)` |
| 5 | numeric columns lie in `[min, max]` of their `GraphSchema` spec, including the hard ceilings `max_stock_*`; flag bytes use only defined bits; canonical zeros hold | `RESTORE_OUT_OF_RANGE(field, slot, value)`; a zero violation is `RESTORE_INVARIANT(canonical_zero)` |
| 6 | ids strictly ascending in nodes, edges, seams, sections | `RESTORE_ID_ORDER(slot)` |
| 7 | each `next_*` is above every id in its table | `RESTORE_COUNTER(counter, max_id)` |
| 8 | every live edge endpoint names a live node of the right section class; no live edge points at a tombstone | `RESTORE_BAD_EDGE_ENDPOINT(edge_id)` |
| 9 | every seam sub-edge has its SeamRecord and every record's lists name rows of the right kind | `RESTORE_SEAM_MISMATCH(seam_id)` |
| 10 | queue lengths within bounds, queue subjects name live rows | `RESTORE_QUEUE(queue, length)` |
| 11 | every `defs` entry the nodes reference is known to the catalog (`ItemCatalog.has`) | `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF(def_id)` |
| 12 | any LS-24 structural check not named above | `RESTORE_INVARIANT(name)` |

**7.3 Out-of-range is hard, a cap tuning drift is not (resolves TR-itemdb-033 against LS-21).** Step 5's maxima are **physical hard ceilings** from `GraphTuning` (the `n_max(c)` of a room is checked in `post_restore`, § 7.4, because it needs `V`; a store's hard ceiling is `max_stock_*`), not the catalog's tunable `stock_cap`. A save whose store content exceeds a **lowered live `stock_cap`** is therefore valid: it restores byte-identically (so `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` still holds and no REBASED cause is needed), and the **stock reconcile**, which runs at the head of every phase 0, clamps `stock` to the live cap, credits the excess to the section's `disc_*` counter (conservation closes), increments `GraphDiag.stock_clamped` (a legal event, **not** a saturation, so the all-zero saturations assertion stands) and emits a diagnostic naming node, old stock and cap. In steady state the reconcile is a no-op loop over the stores. The reconcile is a function of persisted state and the frozen catalog only, so replay stays deterministic. ADR-0016 shares this row: it may prefer the clamp in `post_restore`; this ADR chooses phase 0 because it keeps the restore byte-identical, and states the alternative (Open Question 2). `gdd_sync` carves the case out of LS-21's "never by clamping".

**7.4 `post_restore`** (`GraphDerived.post_restore(ctx)`, runs after Layout's restore because of `restore_after`): **(1)** for each compartment row, look up `room_ref` through the `RoomSource` port; an unknown room is `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_ROOM(room_ref)` for the first such compartment (loud by design, no default `V`); **(2)** check `n_o2 + n_inert` against `P_MAX x V x GAS_SCALE` per compartment, `RESTORE_OUT_OF_RANGE("n_gas", slot, value)`; **(3)** rebuild every DERIVED cache (`ensure_derived()`, including `served_pm`, intensive values and the descriptor store, writing no persisted field and drawing no RNG); **(4)** seed the last-emitted buckets from the restored values and the band and STRAIN memory from the payload (never re-derived from the values), so the first run reproduces an uninterrupted run and the kernel's one `ALL` batch is followed by silence (ADR-0012 owns the phase code that reads the seeds); **(5)** run the structural invariants of LS-24 in every build. Cross-block verifiers (INV-x) and the order among blocks' `post_restore` are ADR-0016's. A fault here fails the whole load (kernel `LOADING` to `FAULTED`), because `post_restore` runs after the swap; ADR-0016 must guarantee a faulted `LOADING` never enters play with the restored world (cross-ADR assumption).

**7.5 Versioning.** `schema_version` is 1 and `supported_versions` is `[1]`. A future shape change registers a pure `(old Dictionary) -> new Dictionary` migration in `graph_restore.gd` and bumps both the version and the committed schema fingerprint in the same commit; retained golden saves in `tests/fixtures/saves/` are migration fixtures (TR-lsg-040, ADR-0006 § 2.6).

### 8. Faults

**8.1 Domain 3 table** (`src/sim/graph/graph_faults.gd`, `class_name GraphFaults`, `DOMAIN_ID = 3`, codes pre-packed `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, append-only, never reused; `NAMES` indexed by local code):

| Local | Name | Raised when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `NOT_IN_SCOPE` | (ADR-0003 § 6's example, kept) a mutator defect that is not the plain `REFUSED` |
| 2 | `RESTORE_BAD_VERSION` | § 7.2 step 1 |
| 3 | `RESTORE_BAD_TAG` | step 2 |
| 4 | `RESTORE_BAD_LENGTH` | step 3 |
| 5 | `RESTORE_BAD_ENUM` | step 4 |
| 6 | `RESTORE_OUT_OF_RANGE` | step 5 and § 7.4 (2) |
| 7 | `RESTORE_ID_ORDER` | step 6 |
| 8 | `RESTORE_QUEUE` | step 10 |
| 9 | `RESTORE_COUNTER` | step 7 |
| 10 | `RESTORE_BAD_EDGE_ENDPOINT` | step 8 |
| 11 | `RESTORE_SEAM_MISMATCH` | step 9 |
| 12 | `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` | step 11 |
| 13 | `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_ROOM` | § 7.4 (1) |
| 14 | `RESTORE_INVARIANT` | step 12, canonical zero |
| 15 | `STRUCT_ENDPOINT` | runtime: an edge endpoint slot out of range or a tombstone |
| 16 | `STRUCT_LENGTH` | runtime: column lengths of a table disagree |
| 17 | `STRUCT_ID_ORDER` | runtime: ids not strictly ascending |
| 18 | `STRUCT_COUNTER` | runtime: `next_id` at or below a live id |
| 19 | `STRUCT_CSR` | runtime: a port run or seam list inconsistent with its edges |
| 20 | `STRUCT_SEAM_RECORD` | runtime: a seam sub-edge whose record is missing |
| 21 | `ID_SPACE_EXHAUSTED` | an infallible mutator would pass `ID_MAX` or a table cap |
| 22 | `DESC_STORE_OVERFLOW` | phase 11 would exceed the descriptor store capacity (§ 9.3) |
| 23 | `STEP_RANGE` | `step_no` would pass `STEP_STAMP_MAX` |
| 24 | `SATURATION` | a numeric soft violation under `strict_numeric` (§ 8.3) |

The detail Dictionary carries `String` keys (`"field"`, `"slot"`, `"value"`, `"expected"`, `"got"`, `"subject"`); a fault is terminal and cold, so its allocation is acceptable.

**8.2 Raising.** `GraphFault` (`graph_fault.gd`) is a `RefCounted` of statics, no state: `raise_in(scope, code, subject) -> int` calls `scope.fault(code, {"subject": subject})` and returns `-code`, so a Class A mutator writes `return GraphFault.raise_in(scope, GraphFaults.ID_SPACE_EXHAUSTED, id)` (ADR-0003 § 5); `raise_ctx(ctx, code, subject, detail)` is the same for `restore` and `post_restore`. TR-lsg-024's `GraphFault.raise(code, subject)` gains the scope or context argument (`gdd_sync`). It never uses GDScript `assert`, which is stripped from release builds (`SIM-11`). "Debug also halts" (LS-24) is the kernel's `FAULTED` rule in a dev profile (ADR-0003 § 9), not Graph code. A structural violation is checked after every topology mutator in debug and tests, in `post_restore` in every build, and every run in debug.

**8.3 Numeric soft violations.** A value above its column maximum or below zero where it cannot be, a conservation drift or a clamped `dT` (LS-24): in release the writer clamps, increments `GraphDiag.saturations[field]` and continues; with `strict_numeric` (injected into `GraphModule.setup()` by the composition root: true in tests and `STRICT_DEBUG`) it raises `GraphFaults.SATURATION` instead. Every Graph test suite asserts `saturations` is all zeros. The two builds differ only after a defect, so the build-mode equivalence of ADR-0003 holds on a clean stream. A legal clamp (the stock reconcile, § 7.3) is not a saturation.

**8.4 Boot codes (domain 2, `ContentFaults`).** ADR-0007 § 2.3 makes every content boot error a domain-2 name and lets owner-named codes follow as data stories land; this ADR lists the Graph's: `GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID` (exists), `GRAPH_BOOT_MODE_ID` (largest mode id above 31), `GRAPH_BOOT_POWER_CYCLE`, `GRAPH_BOOT_STABILITY` (D.12 gas and thermal sums for every template compartment), `GRAPH_BOOT_PRODUCT_OVERFLOW` (D.13), `GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING` (the relations of Section G: `HP_FAIL < LEAK_HP <= HP_OK`, `10 x Q_MIN >= max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP)`, band monotonicity, `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` below the RNG subject field, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` equals the registered divisor, and so on) and the new `GRAPH_BOOT_COLUMN_RANGE(table, column, def_id)` (a catalog value copied into a narrow column exceeds the column's documented maximum). All are BOOT tier (ADR-0007 § 2.4: running with them violated is unsafe or non-deterministic) and are evaluated over post-cast integers by pure functions in `src/shared/graph/`. The content lint of TR-lsg-033 is CI tier (judges authored quality): `GRAPH_LINT_CAP_NEAR` (node or edge count within 10 percent of the caps), `GRAPH_LINT_FRAGILE` (a compartment D.12 sum above 500,000 ppm), `GRAPH_LINT_EQUILIBRIUM` (a heated compartment above 60 C), `GRAPH_LINT_FROZEN_PIPE` (a liquid pipe authored below `FREEZE_ON_MC` without a forced FREEZE), in `tools/ci/content_lint.gd`.
